assumptions.body: The serial delivery recovery design assumes a custom message injected by `pi.sendMessage` appears as an identifiable persisted session entry that can be found after restart. concepts.body: A worker attempt is identified by top-level session ID, worker ID, monotonic attempt number, and a random attempt nonce/generation ID. PID is only a locator; PID plus OS process-start identity and nonce-correlated mailbox/config establish accidental process ownership. concepts.body: A subagent report is the worker's bounded claim about task outcome. The supervisor independently records observed process/RPC facts and derives the canonical terminal status. A valid `completed` claim cannot override cancellation, process exit failure, model error, lost identity, or failure to settle. A valid `needs_attention` claim preserves useful partial work without presenting it as runtime failure. Missing reporting is distinct from process failure.

decisions.body: RPC workers load the normal top-level/global Pi extensions, skills, prompt templates, provider registrations, project context, and tools so custom providers and established project capabilities work without a separate mapping layer. The runtime does not treat child tools as a security boundary and does not maintain a tool denylist merely to restrict authority. Role prompts and task instructions define correct worker behavior, including that workers must not recursively delegate, mutate project-model authority, or perform top-level orchestration unless explicitly assigned.
decisions.rationale: This local runtime is trusted, and clear worker instructions preserve compatibility more simply than reconstructing or denying the top-level Pi capability environment.
decisions.title: Inherit the top-level Pi environment and tools in RPC workers

decisions.body: The worker manager treats the first `agent_settled` event after a completion-triggered turn as acknowledgement of that in-flight completion and schedules the next top-level-session queue item without requiring an explicit disposition tool call.
decisions.rationale: Lower completion-turn overhead is more important than a durable semantic acknowledgement.

decisions.body: When a new Pi session header directly names the launching session as `parentSession`, and no source manager remains attached, the runtime durably and atomically transfers that worker-session and completion queue to the descendant UUID so correction forks and clones preserve live work. Later results and delivery follow the descendant. Unrelated new sessions and ordinary switches do not adopt workers. Transfer receipts and crash reconciliation prevent dual ownership. General transfer to an unrelated session, including correction of a mistaken automatic transfer, is deferred until field use demonstrates the need.
decisions.rationale: Correction forks and clones are common enough that live workers should follow the active conversational branch automatically; arbitrary cross-session transfer is unlikely and does not justify v1 complexity.
decisions.title: Automatically transfer workers to a direct fork or clone

decisions.body: A checkpoint is an attention boundary, not a whole-delta authority transition.
decisions.rationale: This supports broad high-bandwidth reviews without accidentally authorizing agent-authored findings.

decisions.body: Adopt one durable tracked model per repository as authority for intended outcomes and explicitly accepted decisions and commitments, while storing uncertainty and agent-authored objects with clearly non-authoritative state. Humans retain authority over outcomes, priorities, values, and acceptance. Code and tests remain evidence of implemented reality; differences are explicit divergence to reconcile. Detailed model-aware planning and execution reconciliation remains deferred.

decisions.body: Ordinary RPC workers inherit the top-level Pi providers, normal extensions, project context, skills, prompt templates, trust, and every unrelated active tool. At launch, the runtime snapshots the parent active tool names and passes an explicit child set that adds `subagent_report` but omits `subagent`, `subagent_status`, `subagent_inspect`, `subagent_tail`, `subagent_cancel`, `subagent_retry`, all `dag_*` tools, and all `dag_model_*` tools. Worker-role metadata causes this extension's parent entrypoint to return before attaching its worker-session writer, parent result watcher, completion dispatcher, or management UI; only child reporting initializes. The prompt forbids recursive delegation. The runtime does not guess at or deny arbitrary third-party tools, and headless interactive UI requests are answered with cancellation rather than allowed to hang. Nested fanout is deferred; if later needed, it requires explicit opt-in with child-safe routing and depth/cycle limits. This narrows `DEC-ambient-rpc-worker-inheritance` only for parent-owned orchestration and authority surfaces, not as a general security boundary.
decisions.rationale: This uses the established Pi child-role pattern to prevent recursion and duplicate parent services without broadly reducing worker capability.
decisions.title: Inherit normal child tools while omitting parent orchestration surfaces

decisions.body: Input channel does not change semantic authority rules, and no command argument is auto-accepted merely because it started brainstorming.
decisions.rationale: This preserves direct-user commitment without turning `/dag brainstorm auth` into an accidental governing requirement.

decisions.body: Each serial worker completion follow-up is capped at 16 KiB and includes stable completion ID, worker ID/label and attempt, canonical terminal status, report status, bounded worker summary, artifact references, optional next steps, and concise `subagent_inspect`/`subagent_tail` hints. Truncation is explicit. Report details, raw transcript, tool history, diagnostic logs, and artifact contents are never injected automatically; the immutable terminal result remains available through inspection. The first top-level `agent_settled` after this follow-up automatically acknowledges it under the accepted queue policy.
decisions.rationale: Compact identity, status, summary, and references let the top-level agent react without duplicating worker history or consuming unbounded context.
decisions.title: Inject compact worker completions and inspect details on demand

decisions.body: Tools never store raw user wording but mechanically prevent accepted semantic prose/scope/rationale from changing without renewed authority. Explicit batch acceptance identifies exact object hashes.

decisions.title: Defer persistent worker UI until DAG redesign

decisions.body: Workers survive top-level Pi reload and exit through detached per-run supervisor processes, not a centralized daemon. Each supervisor runs in an independent process group and persists only bounded state: repository/run/worker/attempt IDs, an unguessable ownership token, PID plus process-start identity, heartbeat, compact atomic snapshot, structured result envelope, and completion receipt. On reconnect, the extension verifies process identity, restores the DAG and live UI projection, reconciles completed, missing, stale, and orphaned workers, and queues undelivered completions. Raw Pi message, reasoning, tool-delta, and event streams are never persisted.
decisions.rationale: This retains independent worker lifetime with less infrastructure than a daemon while directly correcting the resource, identity, recovery, and UI weaknesses observed in pi-subagents.
decisions.title: Use detached per-run worker supervisors

decisions.body: Explicit unambiguous user direction commits once; silence and agent-derived implications never commit; ambiguity or conflict remains unresolved.
decisions.rationale: This preserves low ceremony and human authority simultaneously.
decisions.title: Direct statements commit; derivations require review

decisions.body: Discovery is an active v1 type during brainstorming, not a dormant execution-only placeholder. Research, repository inspection, prototypes, user observations, and later implementation may produce discoveries. A discovery records a new finding and its possible model impact until the agent integrates it into evidence, assumptions, questions, tensions, proposals, scenarios, decisions, or commitments, dismisses it, or defers it. Future execution reconciliation reuses this same type for worker findings but does not define its existence.
decisions.rationale: Prototypes and research are primary evidence-generating activities during mixed-initiative exploration. Restricting discovery to future DAG execution would lose the finding-to-model-change step that brainstorming already needs.
decisions.title: Use discoveries throughout brainstorming and future execution

decisions.body: Direct requirements may become accepted commitments without synthetic decisions. Derived commitments begin not_reviewed and govern only after explicit acceptance. Decisions link selected proposals and derived commitments without duplicating their prose.
decisions.rationale: This is the smallest split that preserves why, chosen tradeoff, and enforceable contract for different views.
decisions.title: Distinct intent, decision, and commitment

decisions.body: Persist one current tracked snapshot containing materially useful typed objects, including active uncertainty and discoveries. Objects carry stable identity, type-specific state, scope, source/provenance, relationships, timestamps, and confidence where meaningful. Git supplies history; the model is not an event log. Focus-session review/presentation state and scratch research remain ephemeral.
decisions.rationale: Semantic migration rewrite replacing obsolete legacy terminology while preserving the accepted behavior.
decisions.title: Keep one current tracked model snapshot

decisions.body: Generated specs distinguish governing effect from active reconsideration without mixing historical/non-current content into current contracts.
decisions.rationale: This matches the accepted rule that reconsideration does not automatically revoke authority while warning readers about potential change.
decisions.title: Include effective content with an Under review marker

decisions.body: Uncommitted checkpoint deltas are computed by snapshot comparison without writing review metadata into the authoritative model.
decisions.rationale: This supports accurate resume and deltas while preserving the model/presentation boundary.
decisions.title: Ephemeral per-session baseline token/projection

decisions.body: Normative spec inclusion never inherits authority through relationships; every emitted semantic body is explicitly accepted and currently effective.
decisions.rationale: This supports stable vocabulary and representative behavioral examples without smuggling agent interpretation into specs.
decisions.title: Accepted intent, concept, scenario, decision, and commitment are spec-eligible

decisions.body: Focus identity is command-owned, stable, resumable, and never confused with creating another authority model.
decisions.rationale: This preserves convenient interactive use and deterministic automation while making the new one-model semantics visible.
decisions.title: Selector plus new/resume/list/stop subcommands

decisions.body: Cross-workstream links are legal and visible; validators enforce endpoint existence, allowed endpoint types, and acyclic supersession.
decisions.rationale: This supports bounded context without duplicating objects or maintaining reverse-link arrays.
decisions.title: Explicit repository/workstream scope plus typed edges

decisions.body: The next focused exploration must jointly define: the detached worker recovery and reconciliation contract; the exact Pi RPC worker launch, context, and capability contract; and the serial one-at-a-time completion queue contract. Defer live DAG UI detail, model-aware planning/execution restoration, and dependency removal until this combined runtime-contract frontier is coherent.
decisions.rationale: These three contracts share one state machine and establish the canonical runtime projection consumed by later scheduling and UI work.
decisions.title: Explore recovery, RPC, and completion contracts first

decisions.body: Expose an always-asynchronous `subagent` launch tool plus narrow `subagent_status`, `subagent_inspect`, `subagent_tail`, `subagent_cancel`, and `subagent_retry` management tools for the top-level agent. Expose `subagent_report` as the structured child report tool. Equivalent user controls use `/workers list|inspect|tail|cancel|retry`. Remove the dormant `dag_subagent` adapter and do not use `/dag` for generic worker control. This renames the earlier proposed `dag_worker_report` surface without changing the accepted structured-report behavior.
decisions.rationale: The public API should describe the generic owned subagent runtime rather than the deferred DAG adapter.
decisions.title: Use a generic subagent tool namespace and /workers commands

decisions.body: The durable model is the only semantic working state. Ephemeral sessions contain focus, baselines, and presentation packets but no unique project meaning.
decisions.rationale: This preserves continuity and one authority boundary without treating agent-created objects as accepted.
decisions.title: Write coherent findings to the model during exploration

decisions.body: Hot reload, Pi resume, fork, and clone restore the exact focus-session link carried by the Pi conversation branch and keep model brainstorming active after validating the focus file. A brand-new Pi session without a link starts inactive. Forking does not clone, replace, or suspend the focus session. Concurrent interaction with one focus from multiple agents is unsupported and receives no locks, merge protocol, or coordination UX; users are expected not to do it, and stale hash/file conflicts may fail visibly if they do.
decisions.rationale: Pi forks are commonly used to edit an earlier user response and continue the same conversation, so requiring brainstorm reentry would make correction unnecessarily arduous. Supporting deliberate multi-agent use of one presentation focus is not a product goal.
decisions.title: Keep the exact focus active across reload, resume, fork, and clone

decisions.body: Within the trusted local agent and harness threat model, feedback returned through the active Lavish poll protocol is assumed to be human-initiated and is eligible to bind a review-scoped interaction receipt. Do not require an extra Pi confirmation and do not restrict agent-authored rich context to defend against fabricated submissions. Still match feedback to the active review, point, option, and displayed semantic hashes before resolution. Treat accidental automatic submission as a renderer correctness defect covered by conventions and tests, not as an authority-provenance security boundary.
decisions.rationale: A malicious agent or harness already has substantially greater local capability, and the accepted renderer threat model trusts agent-authored local content. Provenance attestation would add friction without defending a material product threat.
sourceRefs: Direct user direction in Lavish renderer review
decisions.title: Treat Lavish protocol feedback as human-initiated

decisions.body: v1 uses a small explicit type union and shared metadata; subtype-specific fields are required only where they enforce material authority or validation behavior.
decisions.rationale: This supports the adopted loop and migration while leaving room to split types after real usage.
decisions.title: Lean typed v1 core

decisions.body: The agent initiates a user-facing review turn when a coherent cluster needs product judgment, evidence materially changes framing, a user preference blocks progress, a contradiction affects governing direction, a material prototype result appears, continuing risks directional drift, the user changes focus or pauses, or the user requests review. A review turn is an attention/presentation boundary—not a Git commit or authority transition—and uses no fixed time, turn, object-count, or token quota.
decisions.rationale: Materiality-based review turns preserve autonomous research and concentrated oversight without checkpoint/commit terminology that implies repository or authority mutation.
decisions.title: Use materiality-based review turns

decisions.body: V1's mandatory safety baseline only drops `message_update`, retains selected final message, tool, lifecycle, and control diagnostics, and caps child diagnostics at 50 MiB per run. Atomic conductor behavior, explicit profiles, structured terminal results, process identity, orphan recovery, idempotent completion, and broader budgets remain separate future decisions.
decisions.rationale: The first implementation should address only the measured logging amplification and avoid bundling broader runtime correctness or resource policy.
decisions.title: Apply only the message-update logging hotfix

decisions.body: V1 marks generated files, renders to a temporary location, supports regenerate-and-compare validation, refuses to overwrite unknown targets, protects hand-authored prototype directories, and reports stale generated files conservatively. It does not require a separate generated-file ownership manifest, manual editable regions, reverse synchronization, or automatic deletion machinery; add stronger ownership metadata only after a concrete cleanup or scale need is observed.
decisions.rationale: The one-way model-to-spec boundary needs basic consistency and file-safety checks, but a manifest and elaborate stale-cleanup protocol are premature defensive architecture before dogfooding demonstrates the problem.
decisions.title: Use minimal one-way projection safety without a required manifest

decisions.body: `subagent_report` is a terminating typed tool. Its worker-authored schema requires `outcome: completed | needs_attention` and `summary`; optional fields are bounded `details`, artifact references, and next steps. The serialized report is capped at 64 KiB, with summary at 8 KiB, details at 32 KiB, at most 32 artifact references, and at most 16 next steps. Artifact paths are references only and are never automatically read or injected. The tool returns the validated report in RPC `tool_execution_end` details with `terminate: true`. The supervisor then waits for `agent_settled` or process termination and writes one immutable schema-versioned result containing stable completion/worker/attempt/config identity, canonical terminal status, report status and optional report, timestamps, process exit/signal, Pi/model stop reason, model/usage, bounded fallback text, diagnostic and artifact references, and result hash. Canonical status precedence is: verified cancellation → cancelled; lost or ambiguous process identity → lost or needs_attention; nonzero process exit, RPC/protocol failure, or model error → failed; settled valid needs-attention report → needs_attention; settled valid completed report → succeeded; settled missing report after repair → needs_attention. A captured completed claim is preserved but never overrides observed failure.
decisions.rationale: A small generic worker claim plus an independently observed runtime envelope is reliable across task types and preserves provenance without DAG coupling.
decisions.title: Use a minimal terminating report and supervisor-derived terminal envelope

decisions.body: Use a repeating Explore, Consolidate, Stress-test, Commit, Project loop. Consolidation presents Added, Changed, Still unresolved, Possible misunderstanding, and consequences; stress-testing adds boundary/failure cases, contradictions, and alternatives. Commit explicitly disposes exact model objects according to their type-specific lifecycle; silence commits nothing. Oversight projects Current understanding, Model delta, Decision ledger, Unresolved frontier, Consequence, Divergence, and Representative slices.
decisions.rationale: Semantic migration rewrite replacing obsolete legacy terminology while preserving the accepted behavior.
decisions.title: Center oversight on model deltas and consequences

decisions.body: The one model contains project-specific projection structure without making it governing semantic prose; no second hand-maintained routing file exists.
decisions.rationale: This supports functional domains and supporting documents that do not map one-to-one to workstreams while retaining one project-description source.
decisions.title: Projection declarations inside project metadata

decisions.body: Tracked specs are deterministic structural projections of model-owned prose; regeneration is drift-checkable and hand edits do not mutate authority.
decisions.rationale: This yields readable specs, stable diffs, and one semantic source without requiring an LLM for routine regeneration.
decisions.title: Model-owned prose with deterministic structural projection

decisions.body: Sessions are disposable attention workspaces over one authority and may coexist without separate project snapshots.
decisions.rationale: This preserves useful context switching and resume UX without duplicating semantic authority.
decisions.title: Multiple resumable sessions; one active at a time

decisions.body: Each top-level Pi session owns exactly one durable serial worker-completion queue and one in-flight completion slot, regardless of how tasks are later related to DAGs or other workflows. Every worker launched for that top-level session enqueues into the same queue. The dispatcher deterministically drains one completion-triggered turn at a time. This is a permanent runtime boundary, not a v1 restriction to one mutable DAG run.
decisions.rationale: The top-level agent is the unit that receives and handles completions; queue scope should follow that agent session rather than DAG runs.
decisions.title: Use one completion queue per top-level Pi session

decisions.body: This extension must implement and own its DAG worker runtime instead of relying on `pi-subagents`. Every worker launch is asynchronous relative to the main agent. Each terminal completion, failure, cancellation, or timeout is durably ingested and reported back to the main agent through a bounded completion message; the main agent never has to block on or manually relay a worker tool result.
decisions.rationale: The prior dependency has produced unacceptable event-log/resource behavior and cannot support the desired DAG-native lifecycle and UI contract.
decisions.title: Own an always-asynchronous worker runtime

decisions.body: The first worker UI is a persistent width-aware ASCII DAG widget below the editor, visible only for an active run and updated from conductor transitions. Nodes show compact status glyphs for blocked, ready, queued, running, passed, merge-ready, merged, failed, cancelled, and needs-decision. Large graphs focus on active and frontier nodes. Full diagram, worker/node detail, bounded output tail, cancel, and retry are explicit commands and narrow tools.
decisions.rationale: This provides immediate DAG-centered visibility with portable, bounded UI behavior before an interactive graph surface.
decisions.title: Ship a passive live ASCII DAG widget first

decisions.body: Package a tested `lavish-axi` version as an optional runtime dependency and isolate executable resolution plus open/poll/end and bounded TOON recognition in one adapter. Spawn through the current Node runtime, support AbortSignal, never call private Lavish HTTP/state internals, and fall back clearly to chat when unavailable or incompatible. Tests use a fake CLI and recorded outputs.
decisions.rationale: Make review behavior reproducible without requiring networked npx at presentation time.
decisions.title: Use a pinned optional Lavish CLI dependency

decisions.body: Content-bound authority is checked per point/object rather than through global optimistic revision rejection.
decisions.rationale: This is safe under content-bound receipts while preserving sparse-response efficiency.
decisions.title: Apply clear unchanged points; preserve stale or omitted points

decisions.body: Discussion state is derived from linked open questions; governing effect changes only through an explicit authoritative transition.
decisions.rationale: This avoids a second review-state axis and prevents casual exploration from destabilizing current contracts.
decisions.title: Keep governing effect until explicit suspension or replacement

decisions.body: RPC workers receive a `dag_worker_report` tool and explicit instructions to call it with their bounded terminal report. The supervisor deterministically tracks whether a valid report tool result was captured. If Pi reaches `agent_settled` without one, the supervisor automatically sends a report-only follow-up instructing the worker to call the tool, then waits for the next settled state. The retry count is bounded by configuration; exhaustion produces a report-missing terminal result with bounded final text rather than inferred success.
decisions.rationale: A hybrid tool-plus-repair flow keeps structured results reliable even when the initial worker turn omits the required report call.
decisions.title: Require worker report tool use with deterministic repair prompting

decisions.body: Clearly labeled read-only status, workers, inspect, tail, validate, and diagram diagnostics may remain solely for pre-cutover artifacts, but cannot create or advance execution. Mutating legacy workflow operations remain removed or unregistered.
decisions.rationale: Semantic migration rewrite replacing obsolete legacy terminology while preserving the accepted behavior.
decisions.title: Retain labeled read-only diagnostics for legacy artifacts

decisions.body: Migration preserves current authority and unresolved direction, not every legacy workflow object; the audit report explains mappings, omissions, and representative-view comparison.
decisions.rationale: This avoids both context loss and historical-object bloat while making the one-time transformation reviewable.
decisions.title: Import current meaning plus a migration report

decisions.body: Add optional `dag_model_present_review` outside the six semantic project-model tools. It presents/resumes/ends the active review through Lavish, marks presentation only from real feedback, and returns bounded feedback to the agent. It never resolves model state or grants authority.
decisions.rationale: Separate presentation transport from semantic authority and allow independent resume/failure handling.
decisions.title: Keep Lavish in a separate presentation adapter

decisions.body: Keep tension as a separate durable type for enduring opposing forces, with active, resolved, deferred, and retired states. Questions remain concrete uncertainties, contradictions, tradeoffs, or reconsideration prompts and may arise from a tension.
decisions.rationale: Semantic migration rewrite replacing obsolete legacy terminology while preserving the accepted behavior.
decisions.title: Keep tension as a separate durable type

decisions.body: Each terminal subagent completion is durably enqueued. When no completion follow-up is in flight, the runtime delivers exactly one completion message to the top-level agent. After the agent finishes reacting to that completion and settles, the runtime delivers the next queued completion, continuing one by one until the queue is drained. Stable completion IDs prevent duplicate enqueue or delivery across reload.
decisions.rationale: Serial delivery lets the top-level agent fully process each worker outcome without simultaneous completion turns, while preserving every completion independently rather than collapsing a burst into one summary.
decisions.title: Drain worker completions through a serial follow-up queue

decisions.body: The projector validates unique canonical placement and visible cross-scope dependencies; duplicated normative body prose is an error.
decisions.rationale: This preserves discoverability and cross-domain awareness without duplication drift or noisy repeated contracts.
decisions.title: One canonical body placement; generated links elsewhere

decisions.body: One durable project model is authoritative per repository; initiatives are scoped model objects, not separate authority files.
decisions.rationale: This preserves one source of truth while allowing independent initiative views and context-efficient execution slices.
decisions.title: One repository model with workstreams/focuses

decisions.body: One attached top-level worker supervisor is the sole writer of a schema-versioned atomic worker-session snapshot through one serialized mutation queue. Detached workers write only bounded atomic mailboxes and immutable terminal results. Attempts bind top-level session, worker, and attempt IDs, a random attempt nonce used for stale-file correlation, PID plus OS process-start identity, config hash, heartbeat, and cwd. Reconnect scans results before mailboxes, ingests each valid result once, restores only matching live workers, and marks proven-dead attempts lost. Launch-ambiguous, stale-live, identity-mismatch, corrupt-artifact, concurrent-owner, and cwd-conflict states fail closed to needs-decision; the runtime never auto-relaunches or signals a process whose ownership is not proven. The nonce is a correctness generation marker, not a security boundary against malicious local code.
decisions.rationale: Fail-closed recovery prevents duplicate workers and PID-reuse mistakes across an unavoidable non-transactional OS spawn boundary without pretending local worker artifacts are a security boundary.
decisions.title: Use single-writer state and fail-closed detached recovery

decisions.body: Expose six action-shaped tools: `dag_model_context`, `dag_model_update`, `dag_model_record_direction`, `dag_model_review`, `dag_model_resolve_review`, and `dag_model_specs`. Context reads narrow slices; update cannot grant authority or rewrite accepted semantics; record_direction is the privileged direct-user authority path; review creates hash-bound packets; resolve_review applies independent fresh outcomes; specs previews, checks, and explicitly recovers projections.
decisions.rationale: Semantic migration rewrite replacing obsolete legacy terminology while preserving the accepted behavior.
decisions.title: Use six action-shaped project-model tools

decisions.body: The owned subagent runtime manages asynchronous worker launch, detached recovery, result reporting, and per-top-level-session completion delivery only. It does not mutate DAG state, compute DAG readiness, gate dependent nodes, launch DAG work, merge worktrees, or otherwise embed current DAG semantics. Completion messages return worker outcomes to the top-level agent, which alone decides how to interpret them and interact with the current or future DAG workflow. DAG integration will be redesigned separately.
decisions.rationale: The DAG workflow needs independent rework, and coupling generic subagent mechanics to its current state model would prematurely constrain both systems.
decisions.title: Keep subagent mechanics independent of DAG orchestration

decisions.body: V1 workers run as child processes through the exact installed Pi CLI in RPC mode, using ephemeral sessions by default. The runtime incrementally parses strict LF-framed protocol records, persists no raw event stream, treats `agent_settled` as terminal completion, sends RPC abort before process-group termination, and supplies explicit model, thinking, trust, context, tool, and extension profiles.
decisions.rationale: Process isolation contains resource failures and preserves installed Pi/provider compatibility while relying on a public protocol rather than another extension's private internals.
decisions.title: Use process-isolated Pi RPC workers

decisions.body: Current understanding is durable shared-agent context but never carries a human acceptance receipt or governing authority; only its latest value is retained.
decisions.rationale: This preserves continuity and comprehension evidence without pretending causal prose is deterministic or human-approved.
decisions.title: One non-authoritative synthesis in project metadata

decisions.body: v1 persists one tracked project-model/model.json current snapshot; Git provides history and tools own atomic mutations and narrow reads.
decisions.rationale: It makes authority visually distinct from disposable .ai runtime data and minimizes the first durable storage implementation.
decisions.title: project-model/model.json

decisions.body: The default tracked projection surface is the current specification tree; oversight views remain on-demand unless a later accepted use case adds one explicitly.
decisions.rationale: This preserves familiar repository discovery without turning attention/session surfaces into a noisy second documentation system.
decisions.title: Track generated specs and prototype index only

decisions.body: Routine successful semantic model mutations synchronize any affected tracked current specs without making a Git commit. `dag_model_specs` remains the explicit preview, check, and recovery path.
decisions.rationale: Semantic migration rewrite replacing obsolete legacy terminology while preserving the accepted behavior.
decisions.title: Synchronize affected specs after model mutations

decisions.body: `reportRepairAttempts` is configurable from 0 through 2 and defaults to 2. The supervisor sends up to two deterministic report-only prompts before finalizing report-missing and needs-attention.
decisions.rationale: Structured report recovery is worth up to two additional model turns by default.
decisions.title: Default to two bounded automatic report-repair turns

decisions.body: V1 does not use one universal authority-status enum; validators derive governing authority from object type, type-specific state, and a valid acceptance receipt.
decisions.rationale: This makes invalid states mechanically rejectable while avoiding mandatory metadata that has no meaning for a type.
decisions.title: Type-specific state with separate authority metadata

decisions.body: Render a versioned `ModelReviewTurnProjection` containing project/focus identity, revision/hash, Current understanding, selected delta/frontier summaries, exact active review content, and optional agent-authored presentation blocks. Generate one self-contained package-owned HTML shell at `.ai/model-sessions/<focus-id>/lavish/<review-id>.html`; preserve it while unresolved, resume interrupted polls, honor user-ended sessions, and end/remove it after resolution. Bundle responsive accessible CSS and standard review controls, permit trusted rich presentation blocks, and return capped prompts plus severe layout/session metadata while omitting DOM snapshots by default. Rely on Lavish's window-level Send to Agent control instead of duplicating a send action at the top of the page. Make option cards self-contained with all prose needed for an informed choice and do not expose serialized authority-payload expanders. Support any number of awareness and decision points in one turn, with independently queued sparse outcomes. Always include an explicit Other radio option so the human can move away from suggested choices. Keep a separate response text box available regardless of which radio option is selected, so the human can add context or modification to a suggested option as well as describe Other direction. Proceed with direct production implementation rather than creating a planning DAG for this bounded slice.
decisions.rationale: The renderer's product frontier and vertical prototype are complete; the remaining work is bounded production integration and end-to-end dogfood, which does not justify a separate planning DAG.
sourceRefs: Direct user authorization to leave brainstorming and implement
decisions.title: Implement the whole-turn Lavish renderer slice

decisions.body: Asynchronous workers must continue running when the owning Pi extension reloads or the top-level Pi process closes, so the top-level agent can be restarted without losing active work. Completion state is retained durably and reported after a compatible top-level Pi session reconnects; this requirement does not by itself require a centralized daemon.
decisions.rationale: The top-level agent may need to restart independently while delegated work remains useful and in progress.
decisions.title: Workers survive Pi reload and exit

discoveries.body: The exact review was created and marked presented through the semantic review tool's chat rendering, but no Lavish review window was opened. When asked to resolve the review, the user reported that they could not see it in Lavish and did not know what they were reviewing. Material review creation and Lavish presentation are separate operations; a chat presentation receipt is insufficient for this user's current review workflow.
discoveries.implications: The extension and restored focus both activate the presentation tool correctly, while the resumed assistant conversation still exposes the pre-renderer callable schema. Reloading or relaunching the same saved conversation is insufficient; a cloned/forked Pi session should force a fresh assistant tool schema while preserving the focus link.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Use `/clone` to duplicate the current active branch into a new Pi session, verify `dag_model_present_review` appears there, then present the exact active review. If a clone still omits it, report a Pi dynamic-tool/schema restoration defect with the two contrasting diagnostics.
discoveries.title: The active worker-runtime review was not presented in Lavish

discoveries.body: After several weeks of real structured-brainstorm use, collect observed prompt failures and successes, then design a separate transcript corpus, rubric, model-variance study, and prompt-regression workflow grounded in that evidence.
discoveries.title: Agent prompt evaluation after field use

discoveries.body: RPC workers inherit the same extension and tools as the top-level Pi session. Without explicit runtime role metadata, a child `session_start` could attach its own completion dispatcher, widget, and worker-session manager or mistake itself for a top-level receiver. A parent-supplied worker-role environment marker and parent/worker/attempt identity can keep UI and completion attachment scoped to the parent while still leaving ambient tools registered and relying on instructions rather than a security denylist.
discoveries.implications: Follow the established `PI_SUBAGENT_CHILD`-style role split: parent services return early in child mode, while child tool activation is handled separately.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Test that RPC child startup creates no parent watcher, writer, queue, or UI and registers only the child side of this extension.
discoveries.title: Ambient extension inheritance requires a worker-role boundary

discoveries.body: Automatic transfer is required for direct correction forks and clones, which are common. Transfer to unrelated sessions—or moving ownership back after a mistaken automatic transfer—remains deferred. The user considers mistaken transfer unlikely and wants field evidence before adding a general adoption protocol.
discoveries.implications: Implement only direct-parent automatic transfer in v1; preserve enough identity and receipts that a later explicit transfer mechanism is possible without prebuilding it.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Reopen only after an observed need to move a live worker session between unrelated Pi sessions or reverse a transfer.
discoveries.title: Arbitrary worker-session transfer is deferred until observed need

discoveries.body: The recovery design used "token-bound" language too strongly. Under the accepted trusted-local threat model, the random value only correlates mailbox, result, control, process identity, and attempt generation so stale files or PID reuse are not mistaken for the current worker. It does not protect against malicious local workers or code and need not be framed as a capability boundary.
discoveries.implications: Rename ownership/capability token language to attempt nonce or generation ID in runtime contracts and tests.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Verify stale-generation rejection and PID reuse; do not add security ceremony.
discoveries.title: Attempt nonce is a correctness generation marker, not a security token

discoveries.body: Prototype passes at spec/prototypes/brainstorm-pi-adapter/scenario.mjs. It demonstrates the accepted adapter and recovery boundaries using a temp project and deterministic fake Pi/UI/domain/renderer seams; final TypeBox, real ExtensionAPI, and actual Lavish engine remain out of scope.
discoveries.title: Prototype Pi adapter and recovery behavior

discoveries.body: The user's concern combines two separate mechanisms. Parent-only services must be inert whenever the extension sees worker-role metadata, regardless of tool use. Separately, the child's active tool set should inherit normal capabilities but omit this extension's recursive launch/management tools and its DAG/project-model tools, while adding only `subagent_report`. This mirrors mature `pi-subagents`: normal tools/extensions remain, the parent extension returns early in child mode, and nested `subagent` exists only through explicit opt-in. It is not necessary to invent a broad security profile or guess at arbitrary third-party tool names.
discoveries.implications: Implement child-role early return and the exact narrow active-tool omission set accepted in `DEC-child-inherits-tools-minus-parent-orchestration`.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Test tool activation, parent-service absence, report availability, UI cancellation, and no nested launch in worker RPC processes.
discoveries.title: Use the established child-role plus recursive-tool omission pattern

discoveries.body: The focus kickoff instructed the agent to classify the original seed normally, and the seed contains unambiguous direction. However, `dag_model_record_direction` rejected it with “No eligible current user interaction for direct direction” because `/dag brainstorm` clears the interaction reference and delivers the kickoff as extension input. The semantic model says explicit command seeds may be authority-eligible, so transport and policy currently diverge.
discoveries.title: Explicit command seed is not currently receipt-eligible

discoveries.body: Run-snapshot mutation, Pi custom-message append, model execution, repository/tool side effects, and acknowledgement are separate transactions. Stable IDs and explicit ack can guarantee idempotent queue state and at-least-once presentation, but cannot guarantee arbitrary top-level agent actions execute exactly once if the process crashes after side effects and before ack. Completion prompts and handlers must inspect current DAG/repository state and make their own actions idempotent.
discoveries.implications: The accepted queue auto-acknowledges on `agent_settled`; it guarantees ordered delivery state, not that arbitrary top-level side effects execute exactly once.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Completion prompts include stable IDs and instruct the top-level agent to inspect current state before repeating actions after redelivery.
discoveries.title: Completion delivery cannot atomically commit arbitrary agent side effects

discoveries.body: The result hash was proposed so a completion acknowledgement could not accidentally refer to a replaced or stale result artifact. Because the worker-session snapshot already binds a stable completion ID to one immutable result path/hash, requiring the top-level agent to echo the hash is redundant. The ack tool can accept completion ID and disposition only, then validate the current bound result internally.
discoveries.implications: Simplify completion messages and acknowledgement tool input; keep hashes inside storage/recovery logic.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Test that replaced/corrupt result artifacts fail internal validation even when completion ID is correct.
discoveries.title: Result hash should remain internal to completion identity and integrity

discoveries.body:
Planning, chunking, and execution integration details remain deferred until brainstorming is dogfooded.

- Planning and chunking assign relevant prototypes: Prototypes are optional supporting context at the workflow level. Planning agents decide which plan sections reference prototypes. Chunking decides which referenced prototypes are required reading for particular nodes or flow steps.

- Planning begins with the relevant functional spec: Planning begins with the spec.md for the product scope named by the user. Use spec/spec.md to orient or discover domains when scope is unclear, then follow explicit links as needed.

- Let execution report discoveries while the conductor reconciles the model: Plans and DAG nodes reference accepted commitment/scenario IDs and generated slices. Workers may return structured discoveries, evidence, affected commitments/views, conflicts, and proposed responses, but cannot mutate human-owned intent or accepted decisions. The top-level conductor integrates discoveries as proposed/reopened model objects, produces divergence/consequence views, and requests human judgment when direction changes.
discoveries.title: Deferred model-aware planning and execution details

discoveries.body:
Renderer architecture, modality, controls, transport, threat model, and validation seams remain deferred; V1 is chat-only.

- Use fixed semantic and factual tangent badges: Tangent cards may use a fixed semantic vocabulary such as Foundation, Risk, Needs clarity, Contradiction, Integration, and Prototype candidate, plus derived factual badges such as open-question count, Deferred, Partially settled, and New.

- Badges are agent-owned and ignorable: The agent may add, revise, or remove tangent badges as quick informational flags. Users do not edit or approve badges and may ignore them. Badges never constrain tangent selection or become canonical specification authority.

- Show every in-scope tangent in a flat frontier: The tangent selection surface lists every Proposed, Tracked, Active, and Deferred tangent in one flat collection with badges. Out-of-scope and Closed tangents are omitted from the default frontier.

- Keep the datastore renderer-neutral and resolve outcomes directly: The brainstorm datastore contains no Lavish concepts and no raw feedback collection. It stores renderer-neutral questions, proposals, review packets, decisions, and lifecycle state. The agent may present a review as ordinary Markdown or send the same packet to an optional renderer. After any response channel, the agent interprets user meaning and calls dag_brainstorm_resolve_review with semantic outcomes only.

- Review next actions may suggest optional Lavish rendering: dag_brainstorm_review may return a non-binding next suggestion to present the packet as ordinary Markdown or send it to an optional Lavish renderer. The renderer and its feedback transport never become datastore concepts.

- Let the agent choose the most useful question-context representation: The complete brainstorm-turn document may still use a consistent optional Lavish renderer whose stable shell owns Current understanding, navigation, question cards, badges, standard choices, comments, and turn-level actions. Within each question/review point, the freeform context section is flexible rather than one mandatory renderer-neutral shape: the agent may use ordinary Markdown, predefined semantic blocks, arbitrary HTML/CSS, scripts, or a linked/generated artifact such as an interactive web UI mockup. The workflow must not force every context section to be expressible in every renderer.

- Treat agent-authored brainstorm context as trusted local content: Do not require fragment sanitization, sandboxing, Shadow DOM, CSS scoping, or a security allowlist for agent-authored brainstorm context. The workflow assumes the user and agent are the local authors/readers. Renderers may still apply ordinary layout containment, diagnostics, or namespacing for usability, but not as a restriction on expressive capability.

- Allow fully interactive agent-authored context: Agent-authored context may include scripts, forms, editable controls, interactive prototypes, custom buttons, visualizations, and direct renderer integrations when they help communicate or test an idea. Renderer-provided review controls remain available for common decisions but are not the exclusive interaction mechanism. Any response delivered through custom context is still interpreted by the agent; verbatim responses and unprocessed submissions are not persisted in brainstorm state.

- Require session-level modality choice, not per-context fallback parity: A context section does not require a decision-complete Markdown fallback and rich rendering may carry modality-specific information. The workflow itself must not require Lavish: when the user or agent chooses a Markdown-only session, the agent provides suitable Markdown, a crude textual mockup, or a link to a separately opened artifact. Behavioral compatibility is chosen for the current interaction rather than imposed on every authored context section.

- Offer a small optional semantic component vocabulary: Provide markdown, callout, code, table, comparison, diagram, and freeform context helpers for common presentation. Renderer-owned review cards, understanding, options, recommendations, comments, navigation, and submission remain convenient defaults. These helpers reduce boilerplate but never limit the agent from authoring arbitrary HTML/CSS/scripts or linked artifacts when a brainstorm needs more expressive context.

- Explore the turn-to-Lavish rendering engine in a separate tangent: Do not settle the detailed renderer test contract inside production validation yet. Create a dedicated tangent for the engine that converts Current understanding, turn shell, review points, standard controls, and freeform question context into a whole-document Lavish artifact and transports submissions back to the agent. Define automated renderer validation after that engine's architecture and seams are understood.
discoveries.implications: The renderer frontier is settled for a bounded vertical implementation: a separate presentation adapter, tested optional Lavish CLI dependency, whole-turn projection/shell/lifecycle, bounded human-initiated feedback, and semantic resolution through existing model tools.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Implement and dogfood a vertical renderer prototype before refining secondary shell components or broader renderer automation.

discoveries.body: After the partially resolved Lavish review left one continuation point, the user selected its recommended option through a fresh direct chat question. `dag_model_record_direction` correctly accepted the exact decision and synchronized the generated spec, but the active review still contains the now-answered point. `dag_model_resolve_review` cannot clear it because the continuation itself was never presented successfully. The model question and tension can be marked answered/resolved, yet the disposable review frontier remains stale.

discoveries.body: `DEC-defer-worker-widget-until-dag-redesign` explicitly supersedes `DEC-passive-live-dag-widget-v1`, but `spec/owned-worker-runtime/spec.md` renders both as governing direction. The projector's `isSpecEligible` checks accepted state and receipt hash only; it does not exclude objects targeted by an accepted `supersedes` relationship. Projection validation also requires every accepted receipt-valid object to retain canonical placement. The same issue leaves older per-run/DAG-coupled worker wording visible beside newer session-scoped DAG-agnostic decisions.

discoveries.body: Implementation exposed and resolved several details that were too small for product-level review: standard controls must carry review, point, option, and semantic hashes; entering freeform text alongside a selected option is a modification, not acceptance; real Lavish output may encode homogeneous warnings as compact TOON tables; resume must render/open when disposable files are missing; user-ended state must survive review rerendering; exact payload disclosure belongs outside radio labels to avoid clipped interactive content; and the browser layout gate catches failures deterministic string tests miss. discoveries.body: The retained legacy `appendEvent` helper reads all of `.ai/runs/<run-id>/events.jsonl`, concatenates one line, and rewrites the entire file for every event. It currently has no call sites because mutating execution tools are disabled, but reusing it in the owned runtime would create quadratic I/O and reproduce the same resource class the new runtime is meant to eliminate. The owned runtime needs bounded append or compact snapshots, not read-concatenate-rewrite logging.
discoveries.title: Legacy DAG appendEvent performs quadratic whole-file rewrites

discoveries.body: The accepted passive DAG widget and its open projection question assume a live conductor-owned `RunState`, readiness frontier, node transitions, and `/dag` mutation controls. The newer accepted boundary explicitly removes those responsibilities from the subagent runtime and defers DAG redesign. The current extension has only static legacy `DagFile` rendering and read-only legacy DAG commands. Therefore the next implementable UI frontier is a generic per-session worker activity surface; live DAG topology should wait for a future DAG adapter and canonical DAG state.
discoveries.implications: Persistent worker and DAG widgets are out of the subagent-runtime scope. The widget contract is revisited only after the canonical DAG schema and adapter are designed.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Proceed with headless worker runtime and explicit commands/tools; keep static legacy DAG diagram read-only.
discoveries.title: The live DAG widget frontier is premature after decoupling subagents from DAG orchestration

discoveries.body: Established implementations either omit the recursive tool by default or bound it with depth/cycle guards. V1 has no need for worker-owned nested queues, routing, or budgets. If field use requires nested fanout later, expose a child-safe `subagent` variant only for explicitly assigned fanout and add depth, cycle, ownership, and completion routing contracts then.
discoveries.implications: Do not initialize nested worker runtimes or expose the recursive launch tool in ordinary v1 children.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Reopen when a concrete delegated task needs child-controlled fanout that cannot be orchestrated by the top-level agent.
discoveries.title: Nested subagent fanout remains an explicit future opt-in

discoveries.body: The legacy flow exposed orchestration as multiple model calls: discover next action, start a node, ask a separate subagent tool to launch, wait for package notification, and record the result in another call. This creates partial states and makes completion delivery dependent on the main agent interpreting tool output correctly. An owned async conductor should atomically claim a ready step, persist worker identity, launch it, ingest one terminal result idempotently, advance/fail the DAG, and wake the main agent with the resulting transition.
discoveries.implications: The generic worker runtime still needs serialized worker-session state, but it must not own DAG transitions. DAG orchestration remains a separate future adapter.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Reuse worker state and completion APIs from the future DAG redesign without embedding DAG semantics in the subagent runtime.
discoveries.title: Owned runtime should replace agent-mediated launch/result choreography

discoveries.body: The extension now owns a process-isolated always-asynchronous Pi RPC worker runtime under `extensions/dag-workflow/worker-runtime/`. It persists one atomic session snapshot, launches detached supervisors, filters child orchestration tools, captures terminating `subagent_report` results, performs bounded report repairs, derives immutable terminal envelopes, recovers with PID/start and attempt-generation checks, transfers direct forks, drains compact completions serially, and exposes generic tools plus `/workers`. The dormant `dag_subagent` adapter and `pi-subagents` dependency are removed. Fake RPC tests cover reporting, repair exhaustion, cancellation, failure precedence, corrupt-result recovery, reload redelivery, direct-fork transfer, retry, and bounded logging; a real installed-Pi RPC worker completed with a valid structured report.
discoveries.implications: The headless owned-worker scope is implemented. Runtime field use can now evaluate prompts and operational ergonomics; persistent DAG visualization remains separately deferred.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Reload Pi to activate the new parent manager in this conversation, then dogfood `subagent` and `/workers` before designing canonical DAG execution state.
discoveries.title: Owned asynchronous worker runtime is implemented and validated

discoveries.body: Pi has no core subagent-summary guarantee. The official subagent example prompts a separate Pi process, collects completed messages, and scans backward for the last assistant text block; absent text becomes `(no output)`. `terminate: true` only makes a structured tool final if the model chooses to call it—it does not force the call. Stronger extensions add prompt contracts, validated result tools, completion guards, or repair turns. The owned runtime's `subagent_report` plus missing-report repair is therefore an intentional reliability layer beyond Pi's example.
discoveries.implications: Do not describe report invocation as Pi-enforced. Tests must cover omission, invalid arguments, report-only repair, and final report-missing fallback.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Keep one bounded repair decision in the active terminal-result review.
discoveries.title: Pi core does not guarantee that a child emits a summary

discoveries.body: `pi-subagents` collects completed child messages and `getFinalOutput()` scans backward for the last non-empty assistant text block, skipping assistant error messages. Foreground completion returns that text, a file-only output reference, an error, or `(no output)`; the background runner can also fall back to raw stdout lines. It does not require a terminating summary tool. Its separate completion guard only detects implementation-like tasks that exited successfully without an observed mutation attempt and can mark those as failed/needs-attention; it does not guarantee summary production.
discoveries.implications: The owned runtime's required `subagent_report` plus bounded repair is deliberately stronger and more deterministic than `pi-subagents` final-text extraction.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Keep fallback final text for diagnostics, but never treat it as equivalent to a valid structured report.
discoveries.title: `pi-subagents` does not force a structured summary

discoveries.body: `dag_model_review` returns the exact review Markdown as a visible tool result, but the Pi adapter marks presentation only when a later assistant text message contains the entire Markdown verbatim. The user responded to the visible review, yet `dag_model_resolve_review` rejected it as unpresented. The manual recovery used the domain presentation marker. Production should recognize the exact tool result/turn delivery itself, or store a tool-result-bound presentation receipt, rather than require a large verbatim assistant echo.
sourceRefs: Live focus review-lavish-renderer-architecture failure and recovery
discoveries.title: Visible review tool output is not recognized as presentation

discoveries.body: Pi's structured-output pattern makes the tool call the final action in that Pi agent run and exposes its typed result to the caller/client. In the owned async architecture, the caller is the detached RPC supervisor—not the already-settled top-level agent. Therefore `subagent_report` itself supplies the worker summary and eliminates any extra child assistant response, but it does not replace durable result writing, parent watcher ingestion, serial queueing, or a later `pi.sendMessage(..., { deliverAs: "followUp", triggerTurn: true })` to wake the top-level agent. The supervisor should still wait for `agent_settled`, persist the immutable result, and close the child RPC process.
discoveries.implications: Describe `terminate: true` only as the child finalization boundary. Keep parent delivery as a separate durable pipeline because launches return immediately and the parent may be closed.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Clarify the active review so it does not imply Pi automatically bridges a terminating child tool result to the parent session.
discoveries.title: `terminate: true` ends the child turn but does not deliver across processes

discoveries.body: The active review framed worker lifetime as session-scoped cancellation versus a durable daemon. Repository inspection of `pi-subagents` shows a real third architecture: detached per-run supervisors survive Pi reload/exit and reconnect through durable files without a daemon. This materially changes the lifetime decision and means the active review should not resolve that point unchanged.
discoveries.implications: The lifetime review was replaced; detached per-run worker supervisors are now accepted governing direction.
discoveries.proposedFollowup: Carry detached process identity, reconnect, orphan reconciliation, and DAG/widget restoration into future implementation planning.
discoveries.title: The worker-lifetime review omitted detached per-run supervision

evidence.body: The renderer owns the stable whole-turn shell; freeform question context may be Markdown, helpers, arbitrary HTML/CSS/scripts, or linked artifacts. Lavish is optional, review state remains renderer-neutral, review presentation blocks/waits through dag_brainstorm_review, submissions return to the agent for interpretation, failures leave review active, and detailed automated renderer tests follow the engine architecture.

evidence.body: `package.json` pins `pi-subagents` 0.25.0 and `extensions/dag-workflow/dag-subagent.ts` imports package-private `src/**` modules for discovery, execution, watchers, notifications, settings, schemas, and state. The current extension entry point does not import or register `registerDagSubagentTool`; dependency analysis finds no importer. The post-cutover runtime therefore does not currently launch workers, but still installs the dependency and retains tightly coupled dead integration code.
evidence.title: Current pi-subagents integration is packaged but dormant

evidence.body: The official Pi subagent example extracts final assistant output and caps parallel model-visible output at 50 KiB. `pi-subagents` supports file-only output references and bounded parent results but does not require a generic structured report. `pi-agent-router` injects only bounded final responses or validated `submit_result` payloads, not full transcripts/tool history. `pi-subagent-lite` uses explicit output-file contracts. These converge on a compact terminal handoff with artifact references while leaving runtime observations and detailed diagnostics outside the parent prompt.
evidence.title: Pi subagent ecosystems favor bounded final results over transcript injection

evidence.body: The official Pi subagent example launches a child with optional per-agent `--tools`; omitted tools inherit normal defaults and there is no dedicated recursion guard. Mature `pi-subagents` is more explicit: it sets `PI_SUBAGENT_CHILD=1`, its normal extension entrypoint immediately returns in children so parent watchers/UI/orchestration never initialize, strips parent-only orchestration skill/history, and does not register `subagent` by default. Only agents whose resolved tools explicitly include `subagent` receive a child-safe fanout extension, bounded by `maxSubagentDepth`. Other normal builtins and extensions remain available unless an agent declares allowlists. `pi-subagent-lite` defaults child extensions to none and supports per-agent tool allowlists. `@mjakl/pi-subagent` inherits parent/default tools and extensions while bounding recursion with depth and cycle guards. `pi-agent-router` uses `--no-extensions` plus explicit delegated extensions as a stronger sandbox-oriented design.
evidence.title: Established Pi subagent implementations separate child role, tools, and recursion policy

evidence.body: Dogfood artifacts demonstrate useful whole-turn sections and controls, but their shell, CSS, JavaScript, option forms, navigation, and queuePrompt wiring were repeatedly handwritten by the agent. This confirms the token/consistency value of a renderer-owned shell while preserving arbitrary agent-authored context inside cards.

evidence.body: A fresh Pi 0.82.1 RPC process loaded the current working checkout explicitly with global extension discovery disabled. `pi.getAllTools()` included `dag_model_present_review` alongside the other six model tools, and the extension loaded without error. The current `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` also resolves directly to this working checkout at commit 14abba7. evidence.body: Lavish 0.1.43 exposes file-oriented open, poll, end, export, and share CLI commands. Open canonicalizes the HTML path and derives a stable session key from it; saving the same file live-reloads the artifact. Poll waits for normalized prompts, user/agent end state, or browser-proven severe layout warnings. Interrupted polls can safely resume because queued feedback persists. User-ended sessions refuse ordinary reopen and require an explicit `--reopen`.
evidence.title: lavish-axi 0.1.43 help and installed implementation

evidence.body: In Lavish 0.1.43, `window.lavish.queuePrompt` posts a prompt from the artifact iframe and `sendQueuedPrompts` submits the queue. Poll normalizes uid, prompt, selector, tag, text, and optional target, but carries no origin or trusted-user-gesture field. Agent-authored scripts share the page and can call the same functions or imitate standard tags. Therefore a poll prompt proves browser-channel feedback was queued, but cannot mechanically prove a human initiated it.
sourceRefs: lavish-axi 0.1.43 injected SDK queuePrompt and normalizePrompt implementation
evidence.title: Lavish poll does not distinguish human-triggered from artifact-script prompts

evidence.body: The artifact receives `window.lavish.queuePrompt`, `sendQueuedPrompts`, and `endSession`. `queuePrompt` emits prompt text plus normalized tag/text/selector/target context; `options.data` is appended as JSON inside prompt text rather than returned as a distinct field. Poll may also return whiteboard references, session-ended metadata, a DOM snapshot, and severe layout warnings. Standard controls should queue one final response per question. A project adapter must cap prompts/bytes and omit the DOM snapshot by default before model context.

evidence.body: Lavish 0.1.43 ships only a `dist/cli.mjs` executable: package metadata declares no main or exports and documents no JavaScript or JSON API. Results are AXI/TOON. Direct server endpoints and state files are private implementation details. A production adapter therefore needs a pinned CLI subprocess seam, bounded output handling, executable discovery, abort behavior, and fake-CLI tests unless Lavish adds a machine API.

evidence.body: The renderer maps every review point into its own card and form, uses point IDs as independent queue keys, and the updated fixture visibly renders two decisions in one turn. Each form has suggested radios, an explicit Other radio, and a separate response box available under every selection. Automated scenarios assert two decision forms, two Other paths, and two independent response fields. The user exercised one decision through real Lavish feedback without affecting the other.

evidence.body: The user-requested prototype under `spec/prototypes/lavish-turn-renderer/` renders a versioned fixture into a deterministic self-contained whole-turn shell; supports Current understanding, delta, frontier, awareness, decisions, exact payloads, and trusted interactive HTML; bounds expanded and compact-table CLI feedback; and exercises fake open/poll/end, missing-artifact open, abort/resume, user-ended preservation, and cleanup. Standard controls carry review/point/option hashes and treat any freeform text as modification. The real Lavish browser audit initially found one unreachable skip link and two closed-details clipping failures; the shell was corrected and fresh polls returned waiting with no layout warnings. Project smoke and deterministic spec checks pass.
