evidence.body: The retained legacy run state has useful DAG/node/step/worktree fields, but `saveRunState` directly writes `manifest.json` and `nodes.json` as two separate non-atomic files; worker records are also direct overwrites. The old launch flow marks an attempt `running` and saves before a separate model-mediated subagent launch, while result ingestion is a later model call that mutates nodes and writes a worker record. There is no run revision, ownership token, process identity, launch receipt, terminal result ID/hash, ingestion receipt, completion queue, or mutation serialization. A crash can leave manifest/nodes inconsistent, a `running` attempt with no process, a live process with no persisted PID, or a duplicated result transition.
evidence.title: Legacy DAG state cannot safely recover detached workers

evidence.body: Node branches and worktree paths are deterministic by run and node, and refresh verifies branch identity plus cleanliness before work starts. This is reusable. However, a node worktree has no active-attempt lease, owner token, or generation. After a crash, automatic relaunch could place two supervisors in the same worktree, and refresh/rebase must never run while an ambiguous or live detached attempt owns it.
evidence.title: Legacy worktree topology is reusable but lacks attempt ownership

evidence.body: An extension can return from a launch tool while work continues, then call `pi.sendMessage` with `triggerTurn: true` and `deliverAs: "followUp"` to wake the main agent after it settles. `pi.appendEntry` stores compact non-context state pointers and custom entries can have TUI renderers. `ctx.ui.setWidget` supports persistent string lines in TUI and RPC, or a width-aware component factory in TUI; updates can be event-driven and request render. `setStatus`, notifications, tool renderers, and commands provide secondary inspection/control. Long-lived processes, watchers, and timers must start after `session_start` or on demand and receive idempotent `session_shutdown` cleanup.
evidence.title: Pi exposes the completion and live UI primitives the DAG runtime needs

evidence.body: Pi 0.82.1 intentionally has no built-in subagent workflow. Its official example implements a foreground `subagent` tool by spawning separate `pi --mode json -p --no-session` processes, parsing selected `message_end` and `tool_result_end` events, propagating abort, limiting parallel work to eight tasks/four concurrent, capping model-visible output, aggregating nested usage, and rendering rich collapsed/expanded progress. Pi's public SDK alternatively exposes `createAgentSession` with in-memory sessions, direct lifecycle subscriptions, tool/model control, abort, and dispose. RPC mode offers strict LF-framed JSONL commands/events, prompt acceptance separate from completion, `agent_settled`, abort/steer/follow-up, session state, and extension UI transport.
evidence.title: Pi intentionally leaves subagents to extensions

evidence.body: `pi.sendMessage` injects a custom message that participates in session/LLM context. With `deliverAs: "followUp"` it waits until the agent has no more tools, and `triggerTurn: true` starts a turn when idle. Custom message details can carry a stable completion and delivery ID. Pi session entries survive restart and are inspectable through `ctx.sessionManager`, while `agent_settled`, `ctx.isIdle()`, and `ctx.hasPendingMessages()` provide drain scheduling signals. These primitives can reconcile a crash after message append by finding the delivery ID in the session branch instead of blindly sending another copy.
sourceRefs: Pi docs/extensions.md: pi.sendMessage, pi.appendEntry, ctx.sessionManager, agent_settled
evidence.title: Pi can deliver one completion turn and persist its message identity

evidence.body: Pi custom tools execute after runtime initialization with an AbortSignal, incremental `onUpdate`, and extension context. A presentation adapter tool can spawn Lavish open/poll, report that the browser is waiting, remain attached to the current agent turn, kill only the poll subprocess on abort, and later resume the same file-keyed Lavish session. Session start/reload hooks can restore focus presentation metadata without starting background resources during extension loading.
sourceRefs: Pi extensions.md custom-tool and lifecycle contracts
evidence.title: Pi tools can host an interruptible Lavish review wait

evidence.body: The official extension resolves the running Pi invocation by preferring `process.execPath + process.argv[1]` when the current script exists, handling Bun virtual scripts, then falling back to a non-generic executable or `pi` on PATH. It launches with `shell: false`, an explicit cwd, model, tools, prompt file, and cancellation escalation. For an owned RPC worker, Pi's `--no-extensions`, `--no-skills`, `--no-prompt-templates`, `--tools`, `--extension`, `--model`, `--thinking`, `--no-session`/`--session-dir`, and context/trust flags can make inheritance explicit rather than ambient.
evidence.title: Pi's official subagent example provides robust CLI resolution and explicit tool selection

evidence.body: Pi 0.82.1 RPC uses strict LF-delimited JSON commands/responses/events. Prompt success means accepted, not completed; `agent_settled` is the reliable semantic terminal event after retries, compaction retries, and queued continuations. Public commands include prompt, abort, state/model/thinking controls, and session inspection. `message_update` contains cumulative partial message data and must be ignored. `message_end`, tool lifecycle events, `extension_error`, and `agent_settled` are sufficient for bounded progress and terminal synthesis. Pi ships a typed `RpcClient`, but only its declaration/build file exists under an unexported internal subpath, so the extension should implement a small protocol client rather than import private runtime code.
evidence.title: Pi RPC exposes the complete worker lifecycle but its client is not publicly exported

evidence.body: Representative extensions expose complementary patterns: `nano-team` uses three spawn/kill/status tools and a debounced animated above-editor chip widget; `pi-subagents-lite` uses async-by-default file output and one batch completion callback but still writes multiple raw diagnostics streams and has no concurrency limit; `@bacnh85/pi-subagent` uses isolated in-process SDK sessions, closed tool allowlists, idle plus hard timeouts, parent cancellation, no recursive subagents, inspectable in-memory threads, and no disk I/O, but accesses private model-registry internals for shared runtime compatibility; `@mjakl/pi-subagent` uses subprocess RPC, bounded rolling capture, settlement events, persistent logical child sessions, depth/cycle guards, and strict output caps; `pi-dynamic-workflow` uses concurrency/budget limits, O(1) append journals, bounded background completion messages, cancellation, and deterministic resume hashes; `pi-agent-router` adds durable task registries, hidden follow-up status turns, fail-closed delegated extensions, retry classification, and compact session attachment; `pi-subagents-lite/FleetView` demonstrates live conversation, steering, stopping, queueing, and below-editor status.
evidence.title: Pi subagent ecosystem converges on bounded lifecycle and compact UI patterns

evidence.body: A field investigation found that Pi `message_update` records carried a tiny incremental `delta` plus `partial` and `message`, where the latter two were duplicate cumulative copies of the complete response so far. `pi-subagents@0.25.0` synchronously serialized and appended every complete update, writing the growing response twice per token update. The resulting sum is approximately quadratic in response length. One measured run had a 388 KiB session transcript but a 188.6 MiB event log: 187.2 MiB from `message_update`, about 486× amplification. A two-character delta produced a 60,542-byte line because it contained the current 30 KiB response twice. Long-running failed agents produced 6–9 GiB logs. A deployed hotfix drops `message_update`, retains final `message_end`, tool, lifecycle, and control events, and caps child diagnostics at 50 MiB per run; active runs then contained zero message updates and only a few MiB of diagnostics.
evidence.title: Cumulative message_update logging caused quadratic write amplification

evidence.body: `pi-subagents` does not run a long-lived scheduling daemon. For each async invocation it writes a JSON config, spawns a separate Node process running `subagent-runner.ts` with `detached: true`, `stdio: "ignore"`, and `proc.unref()`, and records the runner PID plus status/result artifacts. On Unix this creates an independent process group that can continue after the owning Pi process exits. The detached runner launches and supervises the actual Pi child, writes durable status/results, and exits when that run finishes.
evidence.title: pi-subagents survives reload with detached per-run processes, not a daemon

evidence.body: The focus seed reports that `pi-subagents` can explode `events.jsonl` writes and consume substantial resources. Treat this as a high-impact field observation to reproduce and trace against the installed package before attributing the exact cause.
evidence.title: User reports runaway pi-subagents events.jsonl growth

evidence.body: Local `pi-subagents` 0.25.0 launches child Pi in JSON mode and writes every nonblank stdout line to JSONL while also parsing the same events for progress; async execution targets one `<asyncDir>/events.jsonl` across steps and model attempts. `createJsonlWriter` limits each writer instance to 50 MiB but opens in append mode and starts `bytesWritten` at zero, so each step/attempt/process can append another cap to an existing file. The async tracker can allocate and read the entire unread suffix into memory. The package changelog says earlier default JSONL artifacts duplicated Pi sessions and caused 10+ GiB directories; those sync artifacts were disabled by default, while async `events.jsonl` remains part of observability. Current local `.ai/runs/**/events.jsonl` samples are small, so the user's exact incident is architecturally plausible but not reproduced from surviving files.
evidence.title: pi-subagents streams duplicate raw child events into append-only JSONL

evidence.body: The extension starts a filesystem watcher on its global results directory and scans existing result files at load and again after `session_start` establishes the current session ID. Results are filtered by stable session ID (or cwd fallback), deduplicated in memory for a short TTL, emitted through its intercom/completion event path, and then deleted. `session_shutdown` stops watchers/timers and clears in-memory jobs but deliberately does not kill detached runners. Thus a runner can finish during reload and its result is picked up afterward. The in-memory live-job widget map is cleared and does not appear to be reconstructed from running status directories, so status remains disk-inspectable but live UI continuity is weaker than completion continuity.
evidence.title: pi-subagents recovers completion through durable files and a restarted watcher

evidence.body: Pi's official `structured-output.ts` extension defines a typed tool whose result contains bounded machine-readable `details` and `terminate: true`. Pi instructs the model to use it as the final action; termination avoids an extra assistant turn after the tool call. In RPC mode, `tool_execution_end` carries the complete tool result and details, while `agent_settled` independently proves the session-level run has no retries, compaction retries, or queued continuations left. Therefore a supervisor can capture a valid report at tool completion but must still wait for `agent_settled` or process termination before finalizing runtime status.
evidence.title: Pi supports a terminating structured-output tool captured through RPC

evidence.body: `SessionManager.getSessionId()` exposes a durable session UUID, `getSessionFile()` exposes its persisted JSONL path, and descendant headers record `parentSession`. `ExtensionContext.mode` distinguishes `tui`, `rpc`, `json`, and `print`. In TUI mode, `ctx.ui.setWidget` accepts a component factory whose `render(width)` can remain resize-aware and request rerenders. In RPC mode, `setWidget` supports fire-and-forget string arrays but ignores component factories. `setWidget(key, undefined)` clears either form. Session replacement tears down the old extension runtime before the replacement receives `session_start`, so manager subscriptions, timers, watchers, and widget state must rebind per session and captured old contexts are invalid.
evidence.title: Pi exposes enough stable primitives for a session-scoped worker activity surface

evidence.body: A diagnostic Pi process loaded a copy of this exact session with the current extension. After `session_start` restored the focus, `pi.getAllTools()` and `pi.getActiveTools()` both included `dag_model_present_review`. Therefore package loading, tool registration, focus-link restoration, and dynamic activation all work. The remaining mismatch is that this resumed assistant conversation's callable schema still omits the tool.
evidence.title: Restored focus activates dag_model_present_review in Pi runtime

evidence.body: Reusable assets remain: DAG validation and ready-node calculation; node/step/attempt/run state types; worktree setup and merge helpers; prompt construction with plan/chunk/brief context; worker output/session/model/verdict fields; per-worker JSON records; and a deterministic width-aware ASCII dependency sketch. The diagram is static and accepts only `DagFile`, not live `RunState`. The old conductor required the main agent to call `dag_start_node`, invoke `dag_subagent` with returned params, then separately call `dag_record_worker_result`; completion did not atomically advance the DAG. All mutation tools are now disabled.
evidence.title: Legacy code preserves useful DAG and worker contracts without an active conductor

currentUnderstanding.body: The two requested execution items are complete without reviving the disabled DAG workflow. The model kernel now removes explicitly superseded accepted objects from governing/spec projections and reconciles exact direct authority with equivalent active review points, including startup cleanup of preexisting stale review state. The extension-owned headless subagent runtime is implemented: process-isolated Pi RPC children, detached survival, atomic session state, bounded mailboxes/results/diagnostics, fail-closed identity recovery, minimal terminating reports with two repair turns, compact serial completion delivery, auto-acknowledgement, direct-fork transfer, explicit retry/cancel/status/inspect/tail controls, and child orchestration-tool omission. `pi-subagents` and the dormant adapter are removed. Deterministic tests, repeated supervisor/manager tests, package smoke, spec drift, dry-pack, and a real installed-Pi RPC worker all pass. Reload Pi before dogfooding the new tools in this current conversation. Canonical DAG planning/execution and persistent visualization remain deferred.
