proposals.body: The tool supplies state references, and the agent authors the full shell, styles, scripts, controls, and context.
proposals.rationale: This maximizes page freedom but retains repeated shell/control tokens and inconsistent review behavior.
proposals.title: Let the agent provide complete HTML

proposals.body: Every worker launched by this extension runs asynchronously relative to the main agent. Completion, failure, cancellation, and relevant result summaries are delivered back to the main agent without requiring it to block on a worker tool call.
proposals.rationale: This is explicit user direction in the focus seed and a core compatibility requirement for the desired DAG-centered experience; authority remains pending because the command seed was not receipt-eligible.
proposals.title: Always run extension workers asynchronously and report completion
tradeoffs: The main agent needs reliable wake-up and deduplicated completion delivery.
Worker results need bounded storage and replay after reload.
Background lifecycle introduces cancellation and orphan recovery requirements.

proposals.body: Spawn `npx -y lavish-axi` from the adapter and rely on the npm registry/cache for installation and version selection. Parse the current TOON output and fall back to chat on command failure.
proposals.rationale: Keeps Lavish out of package dependencies and mirrors the current skill workflow.
proposals.title: Invoke ambient npx Lavish on demand
tradeoffs: May access the network during a review.
Version drift can break output recognition without a project change.
npm/npx availability becomes an undeclared runtime requirement.

proposals.body: The conductor owns the worker state machine `pending → claimed → queued → running → terminal`, enforces dependency and capacity checks, persists the claim before launch, binds one worker/attempt ID to one process, ingests terminal results idempotently, advances or fails the node, schedules newly ready work, and exposes all transitions through one subscription. The main agent requests run-level actions but does not manually relay launch parameters or worker results.
proposals.rationale: This removes the partial-state windows and agent-mediated choreography in the legacy tools.
proposals.title: Use one atomic DAG worker conductor
tradeoffs: The conductor becomes a critical stateful component requiring transaction and crash tests.
Git worktree/merge transitions must remain separate from process completion.
Concurrent callbacks need one mutation queue per run.

proposals.body: Deliver one custom completion follow-up and treat the following `agent_settled` event as acknowledgement, then immediately schedule the next queue item without requiring an explicit tool disposition.
proposals.rationale: This has lower model/tool overhead and cannot stall because the agent omitted an acknowledgement call.
proposals.title: Auto-ack the in-flight completion when the top-level agent settles
tradeoffs: An aborted, failed, or irrelevant turn may be misclassified as handled.
There is no durable statement of what the agent did with the completion.
Reload/session replacement ambiguity can cause lost handling or duplicate side effects.

proposals.body: When a new Pi session header names the launching session file as `parentSession`, atomically rebind that source worker-session and its pending queue to the new session UUID after proving no attached source owner remains. Redirect later result ingestion and completion delivery to the descendant. New unrelated sessions and ordinary switches do not adopt workers.
proposals.rationale: Workers follow the user's active conversational branch with no manual resume step.
proposals.title: Automatically transfer live workers to a direct fork or clone
tradeoffs: A fork becomes a hidden side effect on worker ownership.
Returning to the parent can no longer receive its original completions.
Transfer needs durable source/target receipts and recovery across a crash midway.
Concurrent or chained forks require arbitration.

proposals.body: Track valid `subagent_report` capture as supervisor state. On the first `agent_settled` without a report, issue a deterministic report-only RPC follow-up that repeats the exact report schema and forbids additional task work. Wait for another settled state; use a small finite configurable retry count and emit report-missing/needs-attention when exhausted.
proposals.rationale: This implements the user's hybrid requirement without scraping prose or allowing an unbounded self-repair loop.
proposals.title: Prompt settled workers automatically when their report call is missing
tradeoffs: Adds another model turn when workers forget reporting.
The bounded retry count still needs a default.
A worker may report stale facts after partial failure.

proposals.body: Standard controls queue prompts naming review ID, point ID, proposed action, option ID, and the displayed semantic hash/payload. The adapter returns only normalized prompts, tags, text/targets, user-ended state, and severe layout warnings; it drops the DOM snapshot unless explicitly requested, caps prompt count and total bytes, and uses Pi truncation metadata when needed. Within the trusted local agent/harness threat model, feedback returned through the active Lavish poll is assumed human-initiated and may create a review-scoped interaction receipt. The agent still interprets all feedback and calls `dag_model_resolve_review`; matching active review IDs and semantic hashes prevents stale or misrouted outcomes.
proposals.rationale: This preserves correction and ambiguity handling while preventing arbitrary DOM state from flooding model context or bypassing semantic review.
sourceRefs: Authority receipt and sparse resolution contracts
proposals.title: Return bounded Lavish feedback for agent interpretation
tradeoffs: Agent interpretation adds a model turn and can ask clarification.
Annotations and custom controls remain less mechanically structured than standard options.
Truncation must never silently turn partial feedback into authority.

proposals.body: Return session/artifact references, session-ended status, normalized prompts with prompt/tag/text/selector/target and whiteboard summary/file references, plus severe layout warnings. Omit the DOM snapshot and server chatter from routine model content; save diagnostics by reference only when needed. Standard shell controls queue stable review-point/proposal IDs and human-readable labels. The agent interprets the packet and calls resolve_review; no transport field is persisted automatically.
proposals.rationale: The packet preserves user intent and precise annotation targets while excluding large page snapshots and operational prose that provide no routine reasoning value.
proposals.title: Return a bounded intent-transport packet, not raw poll output

proposals.body: If explicitly requested, create `spec/prototypes/lavish-turn-renderer/` with a fixture-driven `ModelReviewTurnProjection`, package-owned self-contained shell, standard sparse decision controls, trusted rich-context examples, deterministic focus/review artifact path, bounded feedback normalization, and fake Lavish open/poll/end scenarios. Include one opt-in live Lavish exercise. Do not register a production tool or mutate project-model authority from the prototype. Use the concrete result to refine projection fields, lifecycle states, limits, accessibility, and failure recovery before implementing the production adapter.
proposals.rationale: The broad product direction is settled; remaining uncertainty concerns concrete seams best exposed by a runnable artifact rather than more abstract review.
proposals.title: Build a bounded vertical Lavish turn-renderer prototype
tradeoffs: Adds a short prototype step before production implementation.
Avoids prematurely coupling production code to an untested projection/shell contract.
Must remain bounded and not become a second authority implementation.

proposals.body: Implement a strict LF parser with request IDs and one bounded in-memory record buffer. Discard `message_update` records without JSON object retention or persistence. Normalize only prompt response, `message_end` assistant final text/usage/model/stop reason, tool start/end names plus small path/progress summaries, retry/compaction state, `extension_error`, and `agent_settled`. Replace the worker mailbox at semantic progress transitions; do not write per-event history. Treat process exit before `agent_settled` as failure unless cancellation was requested. After settled, close RPC stdin and wait briefly for exit before verified TERM/KILL escalation.
proposals.rationale: This supplies live status and terminal evidence while obeying the accepted logging hotfix and avoiding the cumulative streaming object allocation/persistence path.
proposals.title: Project selected RPC events into bounded worker state
tradeoffs: Discarded event detail is unavailable for forensic replay.
Tool result normalization must avoid accidentally copying large accumulated payloads.
Protocol corruption needs a bounded diagnostic excerpt and terminal failure classification.

proposals.body: Render each queue item into a bounded follow-up containing completion ID, worker ID/label and attempt, canonical terminal status, report status, worker summary, artifact references, and a concise hint for `subagent_inspect`/`subagent_tail`. Include next steps only when present. Do not inject report details, raw transcript, tool history, diagnostic logs, or artifact contents. Cap the entire follow-up at 16 KiB with explicit truncation metadata; the immutable terminal result remains available to inspection. The first top-level `agent_settled` after this follow-up auto-acknowledges it under the accepted queue policy.
proposals.rationale: The top-level agent gets enough context to react without recreating the resource amplification or context pollution the owned runtime replaces.
proposals.title: Deliver a compact completion message with stable identity and inspect references
tradeoffs: The agent may need an inspection call for substantive details.
A long summary may be truncated below its report limit.
Artifacts can disappear or change after completion unless copied or hashed separately.

proposals.body: Store one atomic worker snapshot per attempt plus bounded result/artifact files. Keep recent progress as a small in-memory ring or fixed-size rotating diagnostic tail only when enabled. Do not copy child message deltas, reasoning, full tool results, or Pi session events into repository or global JSONL. Track timestamps, status, PID, current tool/path, usage, output references, and terminal error as explicit fields.
proposals.rationale: The conductor needs current state and terminal evidence, not a duplicate event ledger. Snapshot replacement makes disk use proportional to active workers rather than event volume.
proposals.title: Persist compact worker snapshots and bounded results, never raw event streams
tradeoffs: Less forensic detail than a full transcript.
Debug mode needs deliberate bounded capture and redaction.
Atomic snapshots require idempotent transition validation.

proposals.body: Use one shared pure renderer over `worker-session.json`. In TUI mode, install a below-editor component factory whose `render(width)` produces at most eight lines and whose cached state is invalidated with `tui.requestRender()` after canonical state or heartbeat ingestion. In RPC mode, send the same projection as conservative 80-column string arrays after semantic transitions. Use ASCII-safe states: `[ ]` queued, `[>]` starting, `[*]` running, `[R]` report repair, `[+]` succeeded pending delivery, `[!]` failed, `[-]` cancelled, `[L]` lost, and `[?]` needs attention. The header reports active, pending completion, and attention counts. At wide widths show up to five task rows with worker ID, attempt, status, age, and bounded label; compact widths reduce fields/rows; very narrow widths show summary plus the highest-priority row. Clear the widget once no active attempt, undrained completion, or attention item remains. Historical acknowledged workers remain available through explicit inspection, not the persistent widget.
proposals.rationale: A single bounded projection is testable, resize-aware in the TUI, usable through RPC, and updates naturally from already-required mailbox/state events without adding a high-frequency timer.
proposals.title: Render a bounded event-driven worker widget from canonical state
tradeoffs: RPC clients receive a conservative fixed-width projection rather than live terminal width.
Acknowledged successful workers disappear from the persistent widget.
Heartbeat frequency controls the coarseness of displayed ages.

proposals.body: Build the turn document as a hydrated framework application with packaged JavaScript and CSS assets.
proposals.rationale: This supports sophisticated components but adds a browser build pipeline, hydration/runtime complexity, and less transparent artifacts.
proposals.title: Ship a compiled client-side application bundle

proposals.body: Generate one self-contained HTML document from package-owned template, CSS, and standard control JavaScript; do not require Tailwind, DaisyUI, or remote assets at runtime. The shell owns navigation, Current understanding, awareness and decision cards, exact authority payload disclosure, recommendations, comments, queue/send actions, and responsive layout. Agent-authored presentation blocks may use Markdown, predefined components, trusted HTML/CSS/scripts, or links to sibling artifacts without a restrictive sandbox.
proposals.rationale: Bundling removes network/version drift and repeated shell boilerplate while preserving the accepted trusted-local expressiveness boundary.
proposals.title: Bundle a stable offline shell and allow trusted rich context
tradeoffs: Arbitrary context can still disturb shell usability, so layout diagnostics and conventions remain useful.
A bespoke shell needs accessibility and responsive tests.
Linked artifacts require relative-path and size safety.

proposals.body: Standardize the current artifact approach around browser-loaded Tailwind and DaisyUI versions.
proposals.rationale: This provides a broad component library quickly but requires network availability and a browser CSS compiler for the standard shell.
proposals.title: Generate a DaisyUI/Tailwind CDN shell

proposals.body: Explicitly expose only `subagent_report` from the worker-runtime extension inside ordinary children. The terminating tool validates and returns a bounded worker-authored report in tool details. The supervisor captures it from `tool_execution_end`, then waits for `agent_settled` or process failure and combines it with independently observed runtime metadata. If the worker settles without a valid report, run the bounded report-repair policy and preserve bounded final text rather than scraping authority or silently declaring success.
proposals.rationale: A structured terminal boundary supports deterministic DAG transitions and completion messages without granting the child DAG or project-model mutation authority.
proposals.title: Use one child-safe report tool with a bounded fallback
tradeoffs: Prompt compliance is not guaranteed, so fallback remains necessary.
The report schema must accommodate non-code research workers.
This makes structured results a future runtime decision even though the accepted incident baseline did not require them.

proposals.body: On each terminal worker transition, atomically ingest the result and advance the DAG, append a compact non-context session pointer, and schedule a short coalescing window. Deliver one `followUp` custom message with `triggerTurn: true` containing all newly terminal workers, DAG transitions, newly ready work, failures, and decision needs. Deduplicate by worker-attempt completion ID so reloads or duplicate process events cannot wake the main agent twice.
proposals.rationale: This satisfies completion reporting without creating one expensive main-agent turn per worker in a fan-out burst.
proposals.title: Persist every completion and coalesce main-agent wakeups
tradeoffs: Completion reporting may be delayed briefly by the coalescing window.
The message must remain bounded and link to artifacts for details.
Exactly-once delivery requires persisted receipt IDs.

proposals.body: Terminal result ingestion advances the node/step and computes newly ready DAG work immediately, but the conductor does not auto-launch work unlocked by that completion until its queue item is acknowledged with a continue disposition. Already-running independent workers continue. Failure, report-missing, conflict, or needs-decision dispositions keep affected dependents blocked.
proposals.rationale: The top-level agent is expected to react to each completion before downstream work consumes it; otherwise serial message delivery would not provide meaningful control over DAG advancement.
proposals.title: Gate newly ready dependent launches until completion acknowledgement
tradeoffs: Burst completions can reduce throughput while the queue drains.
Independent newly-ready nodes may wait even when safe unless provenance is tracked per completion.
The ack tool needs an explicit disposition contract.

proposals.body: Keep the static legacy `dag_diagram` diagnostic read-only. Do not adapt it to worker-session state or add DAG status/control semantics now. When planning/chunk/run is redesigned, define a separate canonical DAG execution projection and adapter that may combine DAG topology with generic worker references without allowing the worker runtime to own DAG transitions.
proposals.rationale: A live DAG requires authoritative topology and execution state that the generic subagent runtime intentionally does not own.
proposals.title: Defer live ASCII DAG topology to the future DAG adapter
tradeoffs: The original DAG-centered visual goal arrives later.
The generic worker widget cannot show dependency relationships.
Future integration must compose two state sources carefully.

proposals.body: Launch one detached, process-group-isolated supervisor per worker or bounded worker group. Persist its ownership token, PID/start identity, state snapshot, heartbeat, result envelope, and completion receipt. The Pi extension may unload or exit; on reload it scans active snapshots, verifies process identity, restores the DAG/widget projection, and ingests completed results. No always-running daemon or IPC service is introduced.
proposals.rationale: This is the missing middle ground demonstrated by `pi-subagents`: workers can survive Pi reload/exit without a durable daemon. An owned implementation can retain that useful lifecycle while replacing raw event logs and strengthening identity, reconciliation, and UI restoration.
proposals.title: Use detached per-run worker supervisors without a daemon
tradeoffs: Detached processes can become orphans and require explicit retention/reaping policy.
PID alone is unsafe because of reuse; ownership tokens and process start identity are required.
Completion cannot wake a nonexistent Pi process; it must be queued durably and delivered on reconnect.
It survives Pi exit but not necessarily machine reboot unless separately recovered.

proposals.body: Move worker processes and scheduling to a repository/user daemon so runs survive Pi reload and exit; Pi sessions attach through IPC and receive completion notifications after reconnect.
proposals.rationale: This maximizes durability for long runs and decouples worker lifetime from the interactive client.
proposals.title: Run workers in a detached durable daemon
tradeoffs: Requires authenticated IPC, daemon discovery, ownership leases, version compatibility, shutdown policy, log retention, and multi-session coordination.
Completion delivery after the owner disappears is substantially harder.
Expands v1 scope beyond the observed need.

proposals.body: Use a schema-versioned atomic `worker-session.json` as the canonical projection, written only through one in-process mutation queue owned by the attached top-level worker manager. It contains a monotonic revision, top-level session identity, owner epoch/process identity, worker attempts, ingested result hashes, and one completion queue. Attempt lifecycle is `queued → claimed → starting → running → terminal`, with terminal outcomes `succeeded | failed | cancelled | lost`, plus fail-closed needs-attention reasons for launch-ambiguous, identity-mismatch, stale-live, corrupt-artifact, or cwd-conflict. Detached supervisors write only nonce-correlated atomic mailboxes and one immutable terminal result; they never mutate workflow or DAG state. Reconnect scans terminal results first, then mailboxes, validates schema/identity/hash, ingests each result and enqueues completion in one atomic worker-session mutation, restores matching live attempts, marks proven-dead attempts lost, and routes uncertainty to needs-attention.
proposals.rationale: This creates one authoritative runtime projection without cross-process file locking, guarantees idempotent result ingestion, and fails safely across the irreducible process-spawn persistence gap.
proposals.title: Adopt a single-writer detached worker-session recovery contract
tradeoffs: The attached conductor remains a single-writer availability point for DAG advancement.
Ambiguous launches require human action instead of speculative retry.
The snapshot rewrites bounded structured state on each semantic transition, though not on streaming events.
Schema migration and corrupt-artifact quarantine need explicit tests.

proposals.body: Write the renderer-owned HTML to `.ai/model-sessions/<focus-id>/lavish/<review-id>.html`. The canonical path gives Lavish stable session identity and live reload. Store only presentation metadata in the ignored focus session: review ID, relative artifact path, status, last presentation hash, and whether the user ended the browser session. Preserve it while the review is unresolved; end and remove it after resolution. An interrupted poll resumes. A user-ended session falls back to chat unless the user explicitly requests reopen.
proposals.rationale: The artifact is disposable presentation state while unresolved meaning stays in the repository model and active review packet.
proposals.title: Use one deterministic ignored artifact per focus review
tradeoffs: Removing a resolved artifact loses the local visual record, which is intentionally non-authoritative.
User-ended state must be tracked to honor Lavish reopen etiquette.
Focus cleanup needs best-effort CLI end plus file removal.

proposals.body: Each DAG step resolves a worker profile containing model preference/fallback, thinking, idle/hard timeout, token/cost/turn budgets, built-in tool allowlist, optional extension allowlist, system prompt, context inputs, cwd/worktree, and output schema. Default to fresh context containing the relevant generated spec slice, plan/chunk, DAG step, acceptance criteria, owned/forbidden files, and prior-step artifact references. Do not expose project-model authority mutation tools or recursive worker launch tools to workers.
proposals.rationale: Explicit profiles make worker capability reviewable and prevent ambient parent configuration from silently expanding authority or context.
proposals.title: Launch workers from explicit role, context, and tool profiles
tradeoffs: Profiles add schema and migration work.
Some project-specific tools need deliberate child compatibility adapters.
Fresh context requires careful task construction.

proposals.body: Leave launch-session ownership unchanged by default, but expose an explicit adopt action from a direct descendant session. Adoption verifies parent linkage, repository/cwd, no attached source manager, and immutable worker identities, then records a durable transfer receipt and changes only completion delivery ownership; running attempt origin IDs remain unchanged.
proposals.rationale: This balances safe defaults with continuity when the user intentionally moves work to a new session.
proposals.title: Allow explicit worker-session adoption by a replacement session
tradeoffs: Adds a transfer state machine and recovery contract.
Partial adoption would be unsafe, so the whole source queue must move together.
The distinction between attempt origin and completion owner complicates inspection.

proposals.body: Use the next focused research/design burst to specify the durable worker state machine, reconciliation algorithm, serial completion queue, and RPC child contract together. Then derive the live ASCII widget from that single state projection and only afterward restore model-aware planning/chunk/run integration.
proposals.rationale: The UI and DAG scheduler both consume the same state transitions. Settling recovery and queue semantics first avoids building a display around transient in-memory state or reviving the legacy multi-call choreography.
proposals.title: Explore detached recovery and conductor semantics before UI polish
tradeoffs: Delays visible UI iteration.
Combines several tightly coupled lifecycle questions in one frontier.
Planning/execution integration remains deferred for one more burst.

proposals.body: Implement the worker runtime inside this extension rather than relying on `pi-subagents`, so resource bounds, async lifecycle, completion reporting, DAG relationships, and UI state share one explicit contract.
proposals.rationale: This reflects the user's explicit seed direction, but the command-seed transport did not provide an eligible direct-authority receipt; preserve it as recommended pending the next authority-capable turn.
proposals.title: Replace pi-subagents with an extension-owned runtime
tradeoffs: Owning process/session orchestration increases implementation and maintenance scope.
Pi-native primitives and ecosystem code may still be reused as evidence or low-level mechanisms.
The migration must avoid silently changing worker prompts, tool access, or isolation.

proposals.body: Persist repository/run/node/step/attempt IDs, an unguessable ownership token, supervisor PID, OS process start identity, config path/hash, heartbeat, and worktree path/branch in the worker mailbox. On reconnect classify each active attempt as terminal-result-present, live-and-matching, missing, stale-heartbeat, PID-reused/identity-mismatch, corrupt, or launch-ambiguous. Ingest terminal results idempotently; attach only to matching live workers; never signal an identity mismatch; and never auto-relaunch into an ambiguous or possibly owned worktree. Route ambiguity, stale live workers, corruption, and dirty worktrees to `needs_decision`.
proposals.rationale: OS process creation and durable claim persistence cannot be made one atomic transaction. Failing closed in the small crash window is safer than duplicate agents editing one worktree or killing an unrelated reused PID.
proposals.title: Fail closed on ambiguous detached-worker ownership
tradeoffs: Some recoverable crashes require human retry decisions.
Process start identity is platform-specific; unsupported platforms must degrade to conservative behavior.
Heartbeat thresholds affect how quickly missing workers are recognized.

proposals.body: Expose an always-async `subagent` launch tool plus narrow `subagent_status`, `subagent_inspect`, `subagent_tail`, `subagent_cancel`, and `subagent_retry` tools for the top-level agent. Expose `subagent_report` as the structured child-report tool. Provide equivalent `/workers` user commands for list, inspect, tail, cancel, and retry. Remove the dormant `dag_subagent` adapter and do not reuse `/dag` for generic worker control.
proposals.rationale: Names should reflect the accepted DAG-agnostic runtime and replace the existing pi-subagents workflow without preserving its private API shape.
proposals.title: Replace DAG-prefixed worker controls with a generic subagent namespace
tradeoffs: Renames the previously proposed `dag_worker_report` tool.
A broad `subagent` name can collide if another extension is loaded.
Separate narrow management tools enlarge the active tool list.

proposals.body: Project the attached top-level session's canonical worker state into a passive string-line widget below the editor. Show a summary header and bounded rows for active, report-repair, pending-completion, failed/lost, and needs-attention workers; clear it when no active, queued, in-flight, or attention state remains. Use event-driven snapshot/mailbox updates rather than a high-frequency UI timer. Provide separate user commands and narrow top-level tools for list, inspect, bounded diagnostic tail, cancel, and retry. Do not display DAG nodes, edges, readiness, worktrees, or merge state.
proposals.rationale: This preserves immediate async-worker visibility without coupling the generic runtime to the deferred DAG redesign, and Pi supports the same bounded string projection in TUI and RPC.
proposals.title: Ship a bounded generic worker activity widget plus explicit controls
tradeoffs: A worker list is less visually distinctive than the desired DAG.
Stable width tiers and recent-terminal retention still need exact values.
Cancel and retry semantics need to follow the canonical attempt state machine.

proposals.body: Search PATH for lavish-axi and otherwise invoke npx -y lavish-axi at presentation time.
proposals.rationale: This avoids package dependency weight but creates version drift, network behavior, and less reproducible integration.
proposals.title: Require a global command or run npx latest

proposals.body: Promote the validated seams into production modules: a domain-owned `ModelReviewTurnProjection` generated from the actual active focus, model revision/hash, Current understanding, selected frontier/delta, and exact active review; optional focus presentation metadata; package shell renderer; pinned optional Lavish CLI adapter; active `dag_model_present_review` tool with present/resume/end; bounded feedback details; exact tool-result presentation receipts; resolution cleanup; fake-CLI tests; and one opt-in real-browser gate. Reuse contracts deliberately rather than importing prototype modules. Production dogfood is complete when one real multi-point model review is generated, presented, responded to, semantically resolved through existing tools, and cleaned up without manual presentation-marker recovery.
proposals.rationale: The broad decisions and first concrete seams are settled; another abstract pass is unlikely to reduce more risk than production dogfood.
proposals.title: Implement the production Lavish presentation adapter from prototype findings
tradeoffs: Production integration will expose additional Pi lifecycle details.
The prototype remains evidence and should not become a runtime dependency.
A user visual pass may still request shell iteration before or during production work.

proposals.body: Snapshot the parent's active tool names at launch and pass a child allowlist containing all unrelated active tools plus `subagent_report`, but excluding `subagent`, `subagent_status`, `subagent_inspect`, `subagent_tail`, `subagent_cancel`, `subagent_retry`, all `dag_*`, and all `dag_model_*`. Load normal extensions, providers, skills, templates, and project context. Worker-role metadata causes this extension's normal entrypoint to return before attaching parent writer/watcher/dispatcher/UI services; only the child-report registration remains. The worker prompt says not to delegate. Do not maintain a brittle list of arbitrary third-party delegation tools; after removing `pi-subagents`, any separately installed orchestrator is governed by instructions. Interactive UI requests are answered with cancellation by the RPC supervisor so they cannot hang the child.
proposals.rationale: This is the narrow established Pi pattern: preserve useful child capabilities, remove only parent orchestration/authority surfaces owned here, and keep nested fanout as an explicit future opt-in.
proposals.title: Inherit normal tools while omitting parent orchestration surfaces
tradeoffs: The launch command uses an explicit tool list even though the policy is ambient inheritance minus a narrow set.
A separately installed third-party delegation tool remains visible unless configured elsewhere.
Future nested fanout requires a child-safe subagent variant and depth contract.

proposals.body: Create one isolated `AgentSession` per worker with an in-memory `SessionManager`, minimal `ResourceLoader`, explicit built-in tools, direct event subscriptions, cancellation, timeout, and disposal. Share or reconstruct model/auth services and keep all worker state in the extension process.
proposals.rationale: This avoids subprocess startup, JSON transport, and disk sessions while providing direct typed events and low-latency progress.
proposals.title: Run workers as in-process Pi SDK sessions
tradeoffs: Worker resource leaks and crashes share the main Pi process.
ExtensionContext does not publicly expose the canonical `ModelRuntime`; ecosystem implementations reach private model-registry fields or reconstruct services, which may miss custom provider behavior.
No OS-level containment and harder orphan diagnosis.

proposals.body: Extend `dag_model_review` with a presentation mode. In Lavish mode the semantic tool creates the review, renders and opens the artifact, waits for feedback, and returns it to the agent; resume/end actions are also folded into that tool.
proposals.rationale: One agent call creates and presents a review and keeps the active tool list at six.
proposals.title: Integrate Lavish presentation into dag_model_review
tradeoffs: Conflates semantic packet creation with an optional long-running presentation transport.
Resume and layout-repair actions complicate the existing review schema.
A CLI failure becomes a failure of the semantic review tool.

proposals.body: Provide a focusable custom TUI surface for selecting DAG nodes/workers, opening live bounded transcripts, steering, cancelling, retrying, and navigating dependency context directly from the graph.
proposals.rationale: This offers the richest operator experience and follows FleetView/thread-viewer ecosystem patterns.
proposals.title: Build an interactive DAG FleetView
tradeoffs: Custom focus, keyboard, resize, scrolling, and lifecycle behavior substantially expand the first slice.
RPC and non-TUI modes need a separate representation.
Live transcript storage conflicts with the goal of minimal bounded event retention unless carefully designed.

proposals.body: Resolve the exact running Pi invocation using the official example's algorithm and launch with `shell:false`, the node worktree cwd, `--mode rpc`, `--no-extensions`, `--no-skills`, `--no-prompt-templates`, and an explicit tool allowlist. Select the parent `ctx.model` provider/id and `ctx.thinkingLevel` unless the DAG step overrides them. Inherit the process environment and normal Pi authentication/config; pass only reviewed extra environment. Explicitly load a tiny child-safe report extension and any profile-approved provider/tool extensions. Default to `--no-session`; allow a token-bound per-attempt `--session-dir` only for roles that need continuation evidence. Project context-file inheritance is an explicit profile switch, defaulting on for trusted implementation worktrees. Never load DAG/model-authority or worker-launch tools in a child.
proposals.rationale: This preserves exact installed Pi/auth compatibility while preventing recursive workers and ambient extension/tool authority.
proposals.title: Launch Pi RPC through explicit isolated worker profiles
tradeoffs: Custom providers need explicit extension mapping.
Some project workflows depend on global skills/MCP extensions that must be deliberately added to a profile.
Ephemeral sessions reduce post-run transcript inspection unless a role opts in.

proposals.body: Bind each worker-session snapshot and completion queue permanently to `SessionManager.getSessionId()` of the launching top-level Pi session. Reload or resume of that UUID reattaches and drains it. Fork, clone, new-session, and switch do not transfer live workers or queue ownership. A descendant may discover and show a bounded read-only notice that its parent session has live or pending workers, but cannot deliver or control them through its own manager. The user resumes the launch session to handle them. Explicit transfer/adoption is deferred unless field use proves it necessary.
proposals.rationale: This directly preserves one queue per top-level session, avoids hidden cross-session side effects and dual dispatchers, and requires no distributed transfer protocol.
proposals.title: Keep workers and completions with their launch-session UUID
tradeoffs: Forking away can leave completions waiting in the original session.
The user may need to resume the launch session.
Read-only parent discovery must remain bounded and cannot expose child transcripts.

proposals.body: Treat Lavish poll results as non-authoritative user feedback and presentation evidence. The agent interprets and summarizes selected reviewed outcomes in Pi chat, then asks the user for one explicit confirmation. Only that Pi input creates the interaction receipt used by `dag_model_resolve_review`. Lavish can still drive awareness, annotations, corrections, navigation, and proposed sparse outcomes without authority. A later trusted-action protocol could remove the confirmation step.
proposals.rationale: This preserves unrestricted rich context and the current mechanical authority boundary without relying on provenance Lavish does not provide.
proposals.title: Require Pi confirmation before Lavish feedback grants authority
tradeoffs: Adds one short Pi confirmation after browser review.
The browser cannot be the sole decision channel in V1.
Safe to ship against current Lavish without upstream changes.

proposals.body: Adapt the existing width-aware ASCII graph renderer to accept `RunState` and decorate each node with stable compact status glyphs for blocked, ready, queued, running, passed, merge-ready, merged, failed, cancelled, and needs-decision. Show the diagram below the editor while a run is active, rerender on state transitions, and use a low-frequency timer only for elapsed-time text. Provide commands/tools for full diagram, node/worker detail, output tail, cancel, and retry rather than making the widget itself a dense control panel.
proposals.rationale: Pi's widget API can present a persistent live DAG without polluting model context, while the existing renderer already handles width, fan-out/fan-in, ordering, and warnings.
proposals.title: Render a live status-aware ASCII DAG widget
tradeoffs: Large DAGs need viewport/summary behavior.
RPC mode receives string lines rather than interactive components.
Interactive cancellation still needs commands or a separate custom surface.

proposals.body: Define `subagent_report` as a terminating tool with required `outcome: completed | needs_attention` and `summary`, plus optional bounded `details`, artifact references, and next steps. It does not require changed files, tests, model/spec IDs, validator verdicts, retryability, or DAG fields. Use schema-level item/string caps and reject a serialized payload over 64 KiB. Suggested bounds: summary 8 KiB, details 32 KiB, at most 32 artifact references, and at most 16 next-step strings. Artifact paths are opaque references and are not automatically read or injected. The latest valid call is captured, though `terminate: true` normally makes the first valid call final.
proposals.rationale: A small common core works for coding, review, and research workers and avoids making every child fabricate irrelevant structured fields.
proposals.title: Use a minimal generic terminating subagent report
tradeoffs: The top-level agent must interpret code changes, checks, and findings from prose when needed.
Task-specific automation gets fewer typed fields.
Optional details may still contain heterogeneous content.

proposals.body: Drop `message_update`, retain final message, tool, lifecycle, and control diagnostics, and cap each child diagnostic log at 50 MiB. Do not make atomic conductor behavior, structured results, idempotent recovery, explicit worker profiles, or other lifecycle constraints part of this baseline decision.
proposals.rationale: This is the smallest direct response to the measured incident and avoids expanding one logging bug into a broad runtime-hardening project.
proposals.title: Apply only the observed logging hotfix
tradeoffs: Other correctness and recovery requirements would need separate decisions.
Detached ownership, duplicate completions, and partial DAG transitions could remain unsafe.
A log cap treats symptoms if another cumulative event type appears.

proposals.body: When the first `agent_settled` arrives without a valid report, send one deterministic report-only RPC prompt restating the schema and requiring `subagent_report` as the only action. If the second run settles without a valid report, finalize as report-missing/needs-attention with bounded final text. Expose `reportRepairAttempts` as an integer from 0 through 2, default 1; never retry task work automatically.
proposals.rationale: One repair turn usually corrects omission while guaranteeing termination and avoiding a report-compliance loop.
proposals.title: Default to one automatic report-repair turn
tradeoffs: A zero setting sacrifices structured completion.
A second configurable repair may spend another model turn.
No repair retries the underlying task itself.

proposals.body: Declare lavish-axi as an optional compatible dependency and isolate open/poll/end subprocess calls in one adapter. Invoke through Pi's abort-aware execution, parse official AXI/TOON output with an explicit parser dependency, and never call private HTTP endpoints. If absent or incompatible, report a renderer error and preserve the active review. Replace this seam if Lavish later exports a stable JavaScript or JSON API.
proposals.rationale: This uses the supported public interface without requiring a user-global install, npx latest/network behavior, or coupling production code to private server routes.
proposals.title: Use an optional pinned Lavish CLI behind a replaceable protocol adapter

proposals.body: Workers continue asynchronously while their owning Pi session is alive. On extension reload or `session_shutdown`, stop accepting launches, gracefully abort children, escalate process-group termination after a deadline, persist interrupted terminal state, flush completion receipts, and leave the DAG resumable through explicit retry. Do not introduce a daemon in v1.
proposals.rationale: Pi explicitly requires session-scoped resource cleanup, and a daemon would add IPC, authentication, ownership, versioning, and orphan-recovery complexity before the core conductor is validated.
proposals.title: Scope v1 workers to the owning Pi session
tradeoffs: Workers do not survive Pi exit.
A reload can interrupt useful work.
Users need clear interrupted/retry status.

proposals.body: Keep a compact status-aware ASCII DAG below the editor and update it from conductor transitions. Use `/dag workers`, `/dag inspect <node|worker>`, `/dag tail`, `/dag cancel`, `/dag retry`, and corresponding narrow tools for details/actions. Hide the widget when no run is active and summarize large graphs around running/blocked/frontier nodes.
proposals.rationale: This keeps the always-visible surface legible and works in both TUI and RPC while preserving explicit auditable actions.
proposals.title: Use a passive live DAG widget plus explicit controls
tradeoffs: Navigation and control require commands rather than direct clicking.
Deep inspection takes another action.
Large-graph focus heuristics need tuning.

proposals.body: Write atomically to .ai/brainstorm/render/<brainstorm-id>/<review-id>.html. Re-rendering the same review updates that file for Lavish live reload. dag_brainstorm_review supports presenting/resuming the existing active review after interruption without creating a new packet. Poll runs in the foreground with the Pi abort signal; interruption leaves review/session resumable. Resolution best-effort ends the Lavish session and deletes the artifact; archive removes leftovers. User-ended sessions are not reopened unless explicitly requested.
proposals.rationale: Path-derived identity avoids Lavish metadata in the datastore, supports one live session per review, and prevents stale ended sessions or historical artifacts from becoming another state/history layer.
proposals.title: Use one derived ephemeral artifact per active review

proposals.body: Treat Lavish as an optional runtime capability. Resolve a package-installed `lavish-axi` executable pinned to a tested version, spawn it through the current Node executable, and isolate open/poll/end plus TOON status recognition in one adapter module. If unavailable or incompatible, report a clear chat-fallback result. Do not call private HTTP endpoints or read Lavish state files. Tests use a fake executable and recorded bounded outputs.
proposals.rationale: Lavish currently offers no public JavaScript or JSON API; one subprocess seam minimizes coupling and prevents ambient `npx` network/version drift.
proposals.title: Use a pinned optional Lavish CLI dependency behind one adapter
tradeoffs: Pinning requires deliberate upgrades when Lavish evolves.
An optional dependency increases install size when present.
Minimal TOON recognition is still a protocol dependency until an upstream machine API exists.

proposals.body: Start/locate the server and use its internal sessions, poll, reply, and end endpoints from the extension.
proposals.rationale: This avoids parsing CLI output but couples production behavior to undocumented routes and server-state details.
proposals.title: Call Lavish server HTTP routes directly

proposals.body: Pass prompts, DOM snapshot, layout data, server guidance, and all metadata directly into the tool result.
proposals.rationale: This preserves all diagnostics but spends context on repeated page structure and operational guidance.
proposals.title: Return complete Lavish poll output

proposals.body: Pass only brainstorm/review IDs and let renderer code query and select whatever it needs.
proposals.rationale: This centralizes projection logic but couples rendering to the datastore and broadens its authority/data surface.
proposals.title: Let the renderer read complete brainstorm state

proposals.body: Define a renderer-neutral `ModelReviewTurnProjection` containing project/focus identity, model revision/hash, non-authoritative Current understanding, delta/frontier summaries selected for this turn, the exact hash-bound active review points/options/dispositions, and optional agent-authored presentation blocks. The renderer receives this projection from the domain adapter and never reads `project-model/model.json` or full focus state directly.
proposals.rationale: A stable input contract lets chat and Lavish share semantic review content while the renderer owns layout and the domain owns model access.
proposals.title: Render from a narrow versioned turn projection
tradeoffs: The projection becomes a versioned API that requires fixtures.
Agents need an explicit way to attach rich presentation blocks.
Large context blocks require size limits or linked artifacts.

proposals.body: Map selected proposal IDs and comments to decisions inside renderer/adapter code and call resolution automatically.
proposals.rationale: This is efficient for simple choices but cannot safely interpret corrections, contradictions, custom context, mixed comments, or changed rationale.
proposals.title: Translate standard controls directly into semantic state

proposals.body: For a single-channel Lavish authority flow, render exact review choices only through package-owned shell controls and disallow arbitrary agent-authored scripts in the same authority document. Rich scripted context must be linked as a separate artifact that cannot call the review queue. The adapter may then treat standard action prompts from its trusted generated document as review-scoped human interactions.
proposals.rationale: Constraining executable context makes the generated authority surface a trusted code boundary despite Lavish lacking prompt-origin provenance.
proposals.title: Restrict authority review surfaces to package-owned controls
tradeoffs: Reverses the accepted unrestricted-context-in-one-document direction.
Rich context and decision controls become separate browsing surfaces.
Still relies on trusted renderer and Lavish package code.

proposals.body: Do not add production renderer code. Continue using the Lavish skill and bash commands to author ad hoc review artifacts when useful; ordinary `dag_model_review` remains chat-only.
proposals.rationale: Avoids dependency and adapter complexity until more dogfood establishes recurring renderer requirements.
proposals.title: Keep Lavish as an agent skill only
tradeoffs: Repeats shell/CSS/control boilerplate and burns context.
No deterministic focus/review resume behavior.
Authority confirmation remains entirely manual.

proposals.body: Write review documents under .lavish/ and retain them after resolution for later browsing.
proposals.rationale: This aids retrospective browsing but creates a second history surface and conflicts with disposable projections.
proposals.title: Keep one .lavish artifact per review as history

proposals.body: Require every `subagent_report` to include task outcome, summary, changed files, commands/checks with outcomes, findings/evidence, conflicts or decisions needed, artifact paths, and retry recommendation. Use optional task-kind variants for implementation, review, and research while retaining a shared core.
proposals.rationale: Rich typing lets future adapters automate more behavior without parsing report prose.
proposals.title: Require rich typed changes, checks, findings, and retry fields
tradeoffs: Workers must fill irrelevant fields or select variants correctly.
The schema begins encoding workflow semantics before DAG and planning redesign.
Model tool-call errors and report-repair frequency likely increase.
Worker claims can be mistaken for observed facts unless every field preserves provenance.

proposals.body: After process termination or `agent_settled`, write one immutable schema-versioned result containing completion/worker/attempt/config identities; canonical terminal status; report status; optional captured worker report; started/ended timestamps; process exit and signal; Pi/model stop reason; model and usage; bounded fallback final text; diagnostic/artifact references; and result hash. Derive status by precedence: verified cancellation → cancelled; lost/ambiguous process identity → lost or needs_attention; nonzero process exit, RPC/protocol failure, or model error → failed; settled with valid `needs_attention` report → needs_attention; settled with valid `completed` report → succeeded; settled without valid report after repair → needs_attention. A captured success claim is preserved but never overrides observed failure.
proposals.rationale: Two-axis provenance prevents a worker's self-report from rewriting process facts while preserving useful partial work and deterministic completion delivery.
proposals.title: Derive one immutable terminal envelope from report and observed runtime facts
tradeoffs: Canonical status derivation needs exhaustive precedence tests.
Usage and model metadata may be incomplete after abrupt process failure.
A result envelope can be needs-attention even though the Pi process settled normally.

proposals.body: Implement server-side TypeScript template/components for understanding, navigation, frontier, review cards, recommendations, Other/comments, queue/submit state, and turn actions. Generate a portable HTML document with package-owned inline CSS and control JavaScript; freeform context may load its own dependencies. Avoid a browser build step and avoid requiring Tailwind/DaisyUI CDN for the standard shell.
proposals.rationale: Generated boilerplate costs no model tokens, works offline, stays visually consistent, and avoids CDN/runtime failure while keeping final artifacts ordinary editable HTML.
proposals.title: Ship a self-contained package-owned shell

proposals.body: Add an optional `dag_model_present_review` tool outside the six semantic project-model tools. It accepts the active review ID and an action such as present, resume, or end; renders the renderer-neutral review projection; opens or resumes Lavish; waits through poll; marks the exact review presented only when browser feedback proves delivery; and returns bounded feedback for agent interpretation. It never resolves review state or grants authority.
proposals.rationale: This preserves the six-tool authority boundary and lets Markdown and Lavish present the same review packet without making Lavish a datastore concept.
proposals.title: Keep Lavish as a separate presentation adapter tool
tradeoffs: A seventh active tool increases surface area.
The agent performs a second tool call after creating a review.
Presentation and semantic resolution remain mechanically separable.

proposals.body: In the same atomic `worker-session.json` mutation that ingests a terminal result, enqueue one item keyed by stable completion ID and internally bound to the immutable result hash. Queue states are `pending → delivered → acknowledged`, with needs-attention for poison/conflicting disposition, and at most one in-flight item. When Pi is idle, inject exactly one bounded custom follow-up containing completion identity and result/artifact references. The top-level agent finishes handling it by calling `dag_worker_completion_ack` with completion ID and disposition only; the tool validates the internally bound result. Only a later `agent_settled` after ack clears in-flight and schedules the next item. Settling without ack leaves the item in-flight and surfaces attention.
proposals.rationale: An explicit semantic ack proves the top-level agent dealt with each completion; `agent_settled` alone proves only that a turn ended and may include abort or partial side effects.
proposals.title: Drain one durable completion at a time with explicit agent acknowledgement
tradeoffs: Each completion turn needs one extra tool call.
A noncompliant agent can stall the queue.
The ack schema and system guidance become part of the main-agent contract.

proposals.body: Persist the attached conductor's random epoch, Pi session ID, PID plus process-start identity, attach timestamp, and low-frequency heartbeat in the canonical run snapshot. A replacement Pi process may take ownership only when the prior conductor is proven dead; if it is live, identity cannot be verified, or concurrent mutation is detected, deny mutation and surface needs-decision. Detached workers and results route by repository/run/attempt identity rather than the original Pi session, so a replacement top-level session can resume delivery.
proposals.rationale: The project does not support concurrent conductors, but top-level restart must work. An explicit lease prevents two Pi sessions from advancing one DAG while avoiding pi-subagents' original-session-only result routing.
proposals.title: Allow one attached conductor per run with fail-closed takeover
tradeoffs: A stale but unverifiable conductor blocks automatic takeover.
Network filesystems and containers can weaken host process identity.
Read-only inspection may remain available while mutation is denied.

proposals.body: Every review rewrites one stable file and continues or reopens the same Lavish session.
proposals.rationale: This minimizes files and supports continuous reload, but ended-session state and old annotations can leak across semantically distinct reviews.
proposals.title: Use one current.html for the whole brainstorm

proposals.body: Make the attached top-level worker manager the only process allowed to mutate one atomic versioned `worker-session.json` containing top-level session identity, owner process epoch, workers, attempts, ingested result hashes, and the serial completion queue. Detached supervisors never edit it. Each supervisor atomically replaces only its own small mailbox heartbeat/status snapshot and creates one immutable terminal result envelope. Startup and filesystem notifications feed these mailboxes into one serialized worker-session mutation queue.
proposals.rationale: Single-writer state avoids cross-process locks and lost updates while allowing detached workers to survive. Atomic mailbox files make disk growth proportional to attempts rather than streaming events.
proposals.title: Use a single-writer worker-session snapshot with per-attempt mailboxes
tradeoffs: The top-level conductor must reconstruct progress from mailboxes after absence.
A terminal result cannot advance the DAG until a top-level process reconnects.
Atomic file replacement and schema migration need disciplined implementation.

proposals.body: Order queue items by terminal result timestamp and stable attempt ID as tie-breaker. No priority lane exists in v1. On the same Pi session, reconcile custom message delivery IDs against session entries after crash. If an item was delivered but never acknowledged and the owning top-level session is replaced, redeliver it to the new compatible session with the same completion ID and a new delivery-attempt ID, explicitly marked as unacknowledged retry. Ack and result ingestion remain idempotent by completion ID/result hash.
proposals.rationale: This matches the user's one-by-one queue, preserves deterministic ordering, and avoids silently losing an item when the top-level session disappears.
proposals.title: Use stable FIFO completion order with same-ID redelivery
tradeoffs: Unacknowledged redelivery is at-least-once handling and may repeat partial agent side effects.
Strict FIFO allows a poison item to block later completions until explicitly dispositioned.
Cross-session session-entry reconciliation cannot prove semantic handling without ack.

proposals.body: Use a bounded structured terminal result boundary so the top-level agent never needs a duplicated transcript. Earlier proposed required fields such as changed files, checks, affected model/spec IDs, validator verdict, and retryability are now candidates rather than universal requirements because the generic runtime is DAG-agnostic. Runtime identity, termination, usage, report provenance, and result hashing belong to a supervisor-derived envelope; worker-authored fields require separate review.
proposals.rationale: A stable result boundary supports DAG automation, model reconciliation, compact context, and reliable retries.
proposals.title: Require a bounded structured terminal result envelope
tradeoffs: Workers need a finalization tool or strict output contract.
Malformed or missing envelopes require a fallback classifier.
Not every research result maps cleanly to changed files/tests.

proposals.body: Launch each DAG worker through the exact installed Pi CLI in RPC mode with an ephemeral session by default. Parse strict LF-framed protocol incrementally, retain only normalized bounded progress/result state, and never persist raw message-update streams. Use `agent_settled` as terminal completion, RPC abort for graceful cancellation followed by process-group termination, and explicit worker profiles for model, thinking, built-in tools, trusted project context, and optional extensions.
proposals.rationale: Process isolation contains worker crashes and memory leaks and reuses the exact installed Pi distribution and authentication path. RPC provides stable public lifecycle control without importing another extension's private source modules. It costs more startup/transport overhead than SDK sessions but better matches durable async worker supervision.
proposals.title: Use a minimal process-isolated Pi RPC worker kernel
tradeoffs: Cold-start and process overhead per worker.
The runtime must implement a strict bounded RPC client and child-process cleanup.
Extension/tool inheritance must be explicit to avoid recursion and compatibility surprises.

proposals.body: Make the first runtime require atomic conductor transitions, explicit worker ownership/profile/context, structured terminal results, idempotent recovery and completion receipts, and compact snapshots. Never persist `message_update`, cumulative `partial`/`message`, reasoning deltas, or raw RPC streams. Optional diagnostics may retain normalized final `message_end`, tool, lifecycle, and control records behind asynchronous bounded writing and a configurable per-run cap defaulting to 50 MiB. Treat token, cost, turn, and aggressive timeout budgets as configurable policy rather than mandatory finite v1 constraints.
proposals.rationale: This directly prevents the measured 486× quadratic amplification and multi-gigabyte failed-run logs without over-optimizing ordinary resource use or weakening conductor correctness.
proposals.title: Target write amplification and durable correctness without broad mandatory budgets
tradeoffs: A generous diagnostic cap still permits moderate disk use.
Optional budgets may allow expensive but legitimate workers unless configured.
Normalized diagnostic schemas require deliberate selection and redaction.

proposals.body: Give each supervisor a bounded atomic control mailbox keyed by attempt identity and ownership token. A conductor writes monotonic commands such as cancel with command ID and reason; the supervisor acknowledges the command in its worker mailbox, sends RPC abort, waits a grace period, closes stdin, then terminates the child process or verified process group if needed. Repeated commands are idempotent. Steering and arbitrary follow-ups remain out of v1 unless separately reviewed.
proposals.rationale: After top-level reload there is no live child-process handle or stdin. A durable command inbox preserves cancellation without trusting PID-only signals.
proposals.title: Control detached RPC workers through a token-bound command inbox
tradeoffs: File polling adds small cancellation latency.
Supervisor failure may still require conductor-side verified process-group escalation.
The protocol needs command retention and acknowledgement cleanup.

proposals.body: The domain supplies one TurnProjection containing brainstorm/revision identity, Initial/Current understanding, active review points and stored options, selected frontier summaries, and explicitly relevant settled context. Each point chooses context kind: Markdown, semantic helper blocks, trusted raw HTML/CSS/scripts, or linked/embedded artifact. The renderer never reads full brainstorm state and the agent never authors the standard document shell.
proposals.rationale: A narrow projection preserves datastore/renderer separation and sensible context use, while explicit context kind lets the engine insert unrestricted material correctly without forcing cross-renderer compatibility.
proposals.title: Render a narrow turn projection with explicit flexible context descriptors

proposals.body: Ask Lavish to expose a machine-readable poll mode and a chrome-owned trusted-action control path that binds a user gesture to opaque action data without making the token callable or forgeable by artifact scripts. If such provenance can be audited, the adapter could create a review-scoped interaction receipt and resolve exact displayed options without a Pi confirmation round trip.
proposals.rationale: This is the only path identified so far to retain unrestricted artifact scripts and make Lavish the sole authority channel mechanically.
proposals.title: Explore an upstream trusted-action protocol for single-channel authority
tradeoffs: Depends on upstream design and release timing.
Browser gesture/provenance security needs careful threat modeling.
Not required for an initial presentation-only adapter.

proposals.body: Define global and per-run concurrency; optional provider/model lanes; FIFO fairness; idle and hard timeouts; turn/token/cost/output limits; process stdout/stderr memory caps; retry classification with bounded exponential backoff; maximum attempts; fail-fast versus continue policy; and circuit breaking after repeated provider/runtime failures. No numeric limit defaults to unlimited in production.
proposals.rationale: An owned runtime must prevent both disk amplification and uncontrolled process/provider/resource fan-out.
proposals.title: Enforce run and worker resource, timeout, and retry policy
tradeoffs: Conservative defaults may reduce throughput.
Provider-specific failures need normalization.
Budget enforcement may yield useful partial work that requires explicit status.

proposals.body: Launch each child with explicit worker-role metadata. The extension's ordinary parent entrypoint returns before attaching worker-session writer, result watcher, completion dispatcher, management UI, or parent commands. A child-specific registration exposes only the structured report surface from this extension. Normal unrelated Pi tools/extensions remain inherited according to the separate child tool policy. Nested delegation is out of v1.
proposals.rationale: Ambient extension inheritance otherwise makes the child indistinguishable from a completion-receiving top-level session and can create duplicate UI/dispatch ownership.
proposals.title: Keep top-level services inert inside RPC worker processes
tradeoffs: The subagent launch tool is visible but operationally unavailable in workers.
Explicit nested delegation would require a separately designed parent-routing contract.
Environment metadata must be validated with the RPC launch configuration.

questions.body: The requirement to survive Pi reload and exit is accepted. Choose the durability mechanism between detached per-run supervisors with bounded durable reconciliation and a centralized daemon with durable scheduling/multi-session coordination.

questions.body: If one top-level Pi session attaches multiple runs, independent per-run queues could trigger competing turns. A session-wide dispatcher can select the earliest pending item across owned runs while leaving each queue durably stored in its run snapshot. If v1 permits only one attached mutable run, this complexity can be deferred.
