scenarios.action: Redeliver the same completion ID after restart. The completion instruction requires inspecting current run/repository state, recognizing already-applied actions, and acknowledging without repeating them. Never generate a new completion ID for redelivery.
scenarios.body: The completion-triggered agent turn merges or edits repository state, then Pi exits before `dag_worker_completion_ack` commits.
scenarios.context: The queue item remains delivered and unacknowledged.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Queue state remains safe and the top-level handler can avoid duplicate side effects, while the system explicitly does not claim transactional exactly-once model behavior.
scenarios.title: Top-level actions commit before the completion acknowledgement

scenarios.action: Write one token-bound cancel command, observe supervisor acknowledgement, let the supervisor send RPC abort and escalate its child locally, then ingest one cancelled terminal result. Only if the supervisor fails and its process identity still matches may the conductor signal the supervisor/process group directly.
scenarios.body: A replacement conductor attaches to a run and the user cancels a matching live detached worker.
scenarios.context: The supervisor identity is verified but the new conductor has no inherited child stdin handle.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Cancellation remains available after reload without PID-only signaling or duplicate terminal transitions.
scenarios.title: Cancel a live worker after the top-level agent reloads

scenarios.action: Queue all four, deliver only the first when idle, wait for its explicit ack and subsequent settle, then deliver the second; repeat until empty. Already-running workers continue, while newly unlocked dependent launches wait for their originating completion's disposition.
scenarios.body: Four workers finish while the top-level agent is busy or closed.
scenarios.context: All four results are atomically ingested and ordered by terminal timestamp plus attempt ID.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Every completion is handled in deterministic order with at most one completion turn in flight and no coalescing.
scenarios.title: A completion burst drains one item per settled acknowledged turn

scenarios.action: On same-session restart, scan session entries, reconcile D into the run snapshot as delivered/in-flight, and do not append another message. If durable visibility cannot be proven, retain the item as unacknowledged and require same-ID redelivery/ack rather than treating it handled.
scenarios.body: A custom follow-up containing delivery attempt D is persisted in the Pi session, then the top-level process exits before marking the queue item delivered.
scenarios.context: The queue item and custom message both carry the same completion ID, result hash, and delivery-attempt ID.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The completion is not silently lost; duplicate semantic acknowledgement remains impossible, and duplicate presentation is bounded by stable IDs.
scenarios.title: Conductor crashes after completion message append but before run snapshot update

scenarios.action: On reconnect, wait a bounded bootstrap grace and inspect the token-scoped mailbox and process identity. If a matching worker appears, attach it. If absence cannot be proven or state conflicts, mark the attempt launch-ambiguous and the node needs-decision; do not auto-relaunch in the same worktree.
scenarios.body: The OS creates a supervisor process, but the top-level conductor exits before its returned PID is committed to the run snapshot.
scenarios.context: The attempt claim and ownership token were persisted before spawn; the supervisor may or may not have written its first mailbox.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: At most one worker edits the worktree, and uncertainty is explicit rather than converted into duplicate execution.
scenarios.title: Conductor crashes between detached spawn and persisted PID

scenarios.action: Do not infer completion from freeform files, do not advance the DAG, and do not enqueue a normal success/failure completion. Quarantine the artifact reference, mark the attempt corrupt-artifact/needs-decision in the canonical snapshot, and enqueue at most one bounded attention completion if its identity can be trusted.
scenarios.body: A detached supervisor disappears and its result file is malformed, hash-mismatched, or bound to a different ownership token.
scenarios.context: The mailbox may be stale or terminal.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Corruption is visible and cannot become an authoritative DAG transition or repeated delivery storm.
scenarios.title: A terminal result is truncated or fails identity validation

scenarios.action: Fail launch validation before claiming/spawning when possible; otherwise classify the prompt/model-selection response as launch failure. Never silently load all extensions or substitute a model unless the profile explicitly defines fallback.
scenarios.body: The parent model comes from an extension-registered provider, but its worker profile does not name the provider extension.
scenarios.context: The child launches with `--no-extensions` and explicit approved resources.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Provider compatibility failures are clear, bounded, and do not expand child authority.
scenarios.title: Selected custom provider is unavailable in the isolated child

scenarios.action: Result ingestion is idempotent, DAG advancement is not repeated, and completion delivery checks the persisted receipt before queuing a follow-up.
scenarios.body: A worker result file is persisted, then the extension reloads before its completion notification receipt is flushed; recovery sees the same terminal result again.
scenarios.context: The worker attempt has a stable completion ID.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Exactly one semantic DAG transition and at most one main-agent completion report occur.
scenarios.title: A terminal result is observed twice around reload

scenarios.body: When the user forks or clones a Pi conversation to edit an earlier response, the exact linked focus session is validated and remains active without requiring `/dag brainstorm` reentry.
scenarios.title: Forking to correct an earlier response preserves focus

scenarios.action: The replacement proves the old conductor dead, takes a new epoch, scans results before mailboxes, ingests each exactly once, advances DAG projections, and enqueues stable FIFO completions. It injects only the first custom follow-up. The top-level agent inspects current state, handles it, calls exact ack with disposition, settles, and then receives the second. Newly unlocked dependent work launches only after its originating completion receives continue disposition.
scenarios.body: A conductor claims and launches one RPC worker, then top-level Pi closes. The detached supervisor finishes, writes a structured result, and exits. A replacement Pi session attaches while two other results are also pending.
scenarios.context: The run snapshot, token-bound mailbox/result files, and completion IDs are valid.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Worker work survives; no raw stream is persisted; no result or queue item duplicates; one completion turn is in flight; and restored DAG state matches disk/process reality.
scenarios.title: Worker completes across top-level restart and drains through acknowledgement

scenarios.action: Apply an explicit session-lineage ownership rule while supervisors continue writing only A-correlated mailboxes and results.
scenarios.body: Session A launches workers, then the user forks or starts session B before they finish. Pi tears down A's extension runtime and initializes B with a distinct session UUID. Detached workers continue.
scenarios.context: Session A owns live worker attempts and a durable completion queue; session B is now attached in the TUI.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Results are not delivered twice or silently attached to B; reopening or explicitly adopting A recovers its queue deterministically.
scenarios.title: A top-level Pi session forks while workers are still running

scenarios.action: Compare PID, OS start identity, token-bound config/mailbox hash, and expected executable. Treat mismatch as identity-mismatch, never signal the process, keep the worktree quarantined, and require a decision before retry.
scenarios.body: After a worker exits without a final result, the OS reuses its PID before the top-level conductor reconnects.
scenarios.context: The mailbox contains the old PID and process-start identity.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The runtime never kills or attaches to an unrelated process and never starts a competing worker in the same worktree automatically.
scenarios.title: A persisted PID now belongs to an unrelated process

scenarios.action: Treat the valid terminal result as stronger evidence than the stale running mailbox, ingest it once, enqueue completion once, and mark the attempt terminal in `run.json`; preserve the stale mailbox for diagnostics until run cleanup.
scenarios.body: The supervisor atomically writes its terminal result and the machine or process stops before replacing its mailbox with terminal state.
scenarios.context: The immutable result validates against the attempt identity and ownership token.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Completion is not lost or delayed by write ordering, and repeated scans are harmless.
scenarios.title: Terminal result exists while worker mailbox still says running

scenarios.body: When the user answers only part of a review and unrelated model content changed, each fresh hash-matching point resolves independently while omitted, ambiguous, contradictory, or stale points remain unresolved.
scenarios.title: Sparse review resolution preserves stale and omitted points

scenarios.action: Do not send the next completion and do not launch work gated by this result. Show needs-attention status and allow the next compatible top-level turn to inspect and acknowledge or explicitly disposition the same item.
scenarios.body: The completion-triggered turn ends, but no matching acknowledgement tool call was committed.
scenarios.context: The item remains delivered and in-flight in the canonical worker-session snapshot.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The queue never mistakes turn completion for semantic handling and never drains past an unresolved completion.
scenarios.title: Top-level agent settles without acknowledging the in-flight completion

scenarios.action: Only the matching live conductor may mutate. The second session remains read-only or receives a conflict; it cannot claim work, ingest results, deliver completions, cancel workers, or take over unless the prior process is proven dead or the user explicitly resolves the conflict.
scenarios.body: A resumed session and an older still-live Pi process both load the same repository run.
scenarios.context: The run snapshot carries a conductor epoch and process identity.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: One serialized state machine advances the DAG; no split-brain completion or worker launch occurs.
scenarios.title: Two top-level Pi sessions attempt to attach the same run

scenarios.action: The conductor persists and deduplicates each terminal result, advances all affected DAG nodes, schedules newly ready work within capacity, rerenders once, and sends one bounded follow-up completion summary after the main agent settles.
scenarios.body: Four ready DAG nodes run concurrently and finish within 200 ms of each other.
scenarios.context: The main agent is still executing an unrelated tool call.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: No result is lost or delivered twice, and the main agent receives one turn rather than four competing turns.
scenarios.title: Several independent workers finish in one burst

scenarios.action: Write the immutable structured result atomically, then mark the worker mailbox terminal. On reconnect, the conductor scans results, validates identity/schema/hash, applies the DAG transition and enqueues one completion in the same run-snapshot mutation, and deduplicates future scans by result hash.
scenarios.body: A matching detached supervisor reaches `agent_settled` and exits while no top-level Pi process is attached.
scenarios.context: The supervisor owns only its mailbox and result path.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The work survives absence, advances once after reconnect, and produces exactly one queued completion without a raw event log.
scenarios.title: Detached worker finishes while top-level Pi is closed

scenarios.action: The conductor classifies the failure, retries or falls back within budget without cancelling unrelated siblings unless fail-fast policy says so, records all attempted models/usage, and exposes partial run status.
scenarios.body: One worker receives a retryable provider error while sibling workers continue successfully.
scenarios.context: The worker profile has bounded model fallback/retry policy and the DAG may allow independent progress.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Healthy work is preserved; failed work is explicit and reproducible; budgets and concurrency remain enforced.
scenarios.title: A worker provider fails during a parallel run

scenarios.action: Preserve the report in the immutable result, derive canonical status `failed`, and deliver a failure completion that notes a captured completed claim is available for inspection.
scenarios.body: The worker calls valid terminating `subagent_report` with `outcome: completed`; the supervisor captures its details, then the child exits nonzero or emits a terminal model/protocol error before `agent_settled`.
scenarios.context: The report is a worker claim, while process and RPC events are supervisor observations.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: No self-reported success overrides an observed runtime failure, and useful summary/artifacts remain recoverable.
scenarios.title: Worker reports completion but the RPC process fails before settlement

scenarios.action: Write canonical terminal status `needs_attention`, enqueue the bounded summary/references, and leave retry or follow-up judgment to the top-level agent.
scenarios.body: The worker cannot safely finish but has useful findings or artifacts, so it calls `subagent_report` with `outcome: needs_attention` and settles normally.
scenarios.context: There is no process or protocol failure.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Partial work is neither discarded nor mislabeled as successful or failed infrastructure.
scenarios.title: Worker settles with useful partial work and needs attention

scenarios.action: The runtime retains only bounded normalized state, triggers idle/hard or output limits, sends RPC abort, escalates process-group termination, records a retryable or final timeout envelope, and applies policy without growing a log indefinitely.
scenarios.body: A child repeatedly emits message/tool updates and remains alive without reaching a terminal response.
scenarios.context: Raw event logging is disabled and the run is at its output/idle budget.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Disk and memory remain bounded; the DAG visibly shows timeout/failure and offers policy-allowed retry.
scenarios.title: A worker emits unbounded progress and stops making useful progress

scenarios.action: Run the bounded automatic report-only repair policy. If it is exhausted, write a terminal result with report status `missing` and canonical status `needs_attention`; do not infer task success or project-model authority from freeform prose.
scenarios.body: Pi emits final assistant `message_end` and `agent_settled`, but no valid `subagent_report` envelope was captured.
scenarios.context: The supervisor retained bounded final text, usage, model, stop reason, and report-attempt diagnostics.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Useful work remains inspectable without letting unstructured prose silently become a successful structured completion.
scenarios.title: A worker settles without calling the report tool

tensions.body: The older accepted widget requires live DAG state and conductor transitions. The newer accepted boundary says the subagent runtime must not own or infer those concepts and that DAG integration will be redesigned separately. Both goals can survive only by splitting a generic worker activity widget now from a later DAG adapter, or by deferring all UI until that adapter exists.
tensions.title: Accepted live DAG widget versus newer DAG-agnostic worker boundary

tensions.body: An explicit agent-only ack tool adds one call but binds a durable disposition to the stable completion ID; result integrity is checked internally and no hash is echoed by the agent. Automatic ack on `agent_settled` is simpler but cannot prove the worker outcome was actually handled, especially after aborts, failures, reloads, or partial side effects.
tensions.title: Explicit completion acknowledgement versus automatic settled acknowledgement

tensions.body: A minimal terminating report is reliable across worker roles and preserves DAG independence, but the top-level agent must interpret its prose. A rich report supports future automation, but burdens generic workers and prematurely encodes implementation/review/DAG concepts. Runtime-observed facts should remain outside either worker-authored schema.
tensions.title: Minimal generic report versus rich typed workflow report

tensions.body: A passive widget plus commands is small, durable, and portable. An interactive graph/thread surface is more discoverable and powerful but adds substantial TUI complexity and pressure to retain more live transcript detail.
tensions.title: Passive DAG widget versus interactive FleetView

tensions.body: The accepted renderer boundary allows trusted agent-authored HTML, scripts, forms, and custom controls, but human authority requires that agent code cannot manufacture an eligible acceptance interaction. Lavish currently gives artifact scripts and visible controls the same queuePrompt channel with no trusted-gesture provenance. Preserving both unrestricted scripting and direct browser-to-authority resolution is therefore unsafe without another confirmation or protocol boundary.
tensions.title: Unrestricted rich context versus mechanically trustworthy authority input

tensions.body: The measured incident requires eliminating cumulative streaming-event persistence and bounding diagnostics. A broader baseline additionally makes all concurrency, timeout, token, cost, turn, output, and attempt limits finite from v1. The targeted option keeps conductor correctness mandatory but allows ordinary resource budgets to remain configurable.
tensions.title: Targeted amplification safety versus broad mandatory resource budgets

tensions.body: Keeping results with the launching session is deterministic and matches the accepted queue boundary but interrupts continuity after a fork. Automatic transfer follows the user's active branch but adds hidden ownership mutation and crash/concurrency hazards. Explicit adoption is visible but requires a new transfer protocol.
tensions.title: Worker continuity across forks versus strict session-local ownership

tensions.body: A subprocess RPC worker has stronger fault/resource isolation and exact CLI compatibility but higher startup and protocol cost. An in-process SDK worker avoids raw transport and disk I/O but shares failure/resource domains and currently has a public-API gap for reusing the parent extension's exact model runtime and custom providers.
tensions.title: Worker process isolation versus in-process SDK efficiency

tensions.body: Session-scoped cancellation no longer satisfies the accepted durability requirement. Detached per-run supervisors survive reload/exit through bounded durable state without a service, but require process identity, orphan reconciliation, and reconnect delivery. A daemon adds centralized durable scheduling and cross-session coordination at the cost of authenticated IPC and a separate lifecycle.
tensions.title: Session-scoped workers versus daemon durability
